## Goal Thalvi gets its first fuzz targets, so code that reads outside input (spoken text, the settings file, recognizer frames) is tested with millions of malformed inputs, not only the cases someone thought of. ## In Short A new `fuzz/` crate holds four `cargo-fuzz` targets. Each one feeds random bytes into one function that handles outside input and fails on any panic, hang or memory error. A short run of every target joins the Heavy workflow so they keep building. Long runs happen in the pre-release break-it run (companion issue). Nothing changes for the user except fewer crashes. ```mermaid flowchart LR F[libFuzzer: random and mutated bytes] --> T1[tasks::decide
spoken commands] F --> T2[numbers::format + writing::normalize
spoken numbers] F --> T3[DesktopConfig::from_json_str
settings file] F --> T4[thalvi_asr::parse_event
recognizer frames] T1 & T2 & T3 & T4 --> R{panic, hang,
ASan error?} R -- yes --> C[crash input in fuzz/artifacts, run fails] R -- no --> K[corpus grows] ``` ## Problem & Current Context - No fuzzing exists. Only two modules use `proptest` (`thalvi-app/src/runner/controls.rs:689`, `thalvi-desktop/src/hold.rs:1662`). `.cargo/config.toml` fixes `PROPTEST_CASES = "256"`. - Mutation testing (Heavy, `.cargo/mutants.toml`) checks that tests notice changed code. It does not throw unexpected input at parsers. - Candidates found by reading the code, all `pub` and callable in-process: - `thalvi_desktop::tasks::decide(text: &str, scripts: &[Script])` (`tasks.rs:43`): byte slicing after case-folding in `strip_prefix_ignore_case` (`:105`) and `spoken_url` (`:123`, `text[..4]` at `:127`). `to_lowercase()` can change byte lengths on non-ASCII text. - `thalvi_desktop::numbers::format(text, Option, words)` (`numbers.rs:71`) and `writing::normalize(&str)` (`writing.rs:85`): `text[begin..]` after `to_lowercase()` (`numbers.rs:102`, `:145`), `words[at..]` (`:398`, `:413`). - `thalvi_desktop::config::DesktopConfig::from_json_str(&str)` (`config.rs:680`): serde with `deny_unknown_fields` and custom validating deserializers. - `thalvi_asr::parse_event(&str)` (re-exported in `thalvi-asr/src/lib.rs:5`, defined in `client.rs:244`): recognizer frames from the network. - The toolchain is pinned to stable `1.99.0` (`rust-toolchain.toml`); `cargo-fuzz` needs nightly. ## Specification - **Crate:** a top-level `fuzz/` crate (not under `crates/`, which is flat and holds only product crates, AGENTS.md:76), with its own `[workspace]` table so the root workspace and `cargo lint --workspace` do not include it. It depends on `thalvi-desktop` and `thalvi-asr` by path, plus `libfuzzer-sys` and `arbitrary` (reason stated in the PR, AGENTS.md:103). - **Toolchain:** `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml` pins a dated nightly. The root toolchain stays `1.99.0`. - **Targets**, one file each in `fuzz/fuzz_targets/`: - `tasks_decide`: arbitrary text plus an arbitrary list of `Script`s (phrases and actions built with `arbitrary`), into `decide`. The result is not checked; only no panic. - `spoken_numbers`: arbitrary text, language (none, `en`, `de`) and word list, into `numbers::format`, and the text into `writing::normalize`. - `config_json`: arbitrary UTF-8 into `DesktopConfig::from_json_str`. When it parses, serializing and parsing again gives an equal config, if the type supports that today. Otherwise only no panic, and the PR says so. - `asr_frame`: arbitrary UTF-8 into `parse_event`. - **Seeds:** each target gets a small text seed corpus in `fuzz/corpus//`: a few real inputs taken from existing tests (a settings JSON, a few spoken phrases, a recognizer frame). Generated corpora and crash artifacts are git-ignored (AGENTS.md: no logs or data in git). A crash input is committed only as a minimal text regression test in the crate it belongs to. - **Lints:** fuzz targets follow the repo's rules: `//!` header, `#[expect(..., reason = ...)]` where a lint must yield, no `#[allow]`. - **CI:** Heavy gets a `fuzz` job that installs the pinned nightly and `cargo-fuzz`, builds all targets, and runs each for 60 s (`-max_total_time=60`) from its seed corpus. A crash fails the job and uploads the crash input as an artifact. PR CI does not run it. - **Found crashes:** a crash found while building this issue is filed as its own `fix(desktop)` issue with the input, the stack trace and the target. It is not fixed in this PR, unless the fix is one line and comes with a regression test. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `cargo + fuzz build` (run from `fuzz/`) builds all four targets. `cargo lint` and the root workspace build are unchanged (the gates pass). - [ ] Each target runs for 5 minutes under `dev-job` (`cargo fuzz run -- -max_total_time=300`). The PR lists for each target: executions per second, final coverage (`cov:`) and crashes found (with the follow-up issue numbers). - [ ] Each target actually reaches its function: a throwaway local run with a deliberate `panic!` added at the top of the target function crashes within seconds. The panic is not committed; the PR states the check was done. - [ ] The Heavy `fuzz` job passes on a `workflow_dispatch` run of the PR branch (`gh workflow run heavy.yml --ref `), and its log shows all four targets ran for 60 s. - [ ] `git status` after a fuzz run shows no generated corpus or artifact files (the ignore rules work). - [ ] AGENTS.md gets one line on where fuzz targets live and how to run one, in the same PR. ## Sub-issues / Related - Start after #727 lands: its PR #731 changes `config.rs`, `writing.rs` and `secondary.rs` (which defines `Language`). - Companion: #733, the pre-release break-it run, runs these targets for hours. - Origin: https://gitea.tailacaa87.ts.net/cybrex/Ideas/issues/68

## Goal
PRs get a fast answer. Mutation testing runs on `main`, and a real failure there files one issue for the dispatcher.

## In Short
Today mutation testing runs on every Rust PR. After this, a PR runs build, lint, Windows and the tests its change affects. Mutation testing runs when something lands on `main`, nightly and on request. It still only advises: survivors appear in the run summary. A green heavy run moves a `verified` tag as a pointer. A real failure opens one issue naming the commits since `verified`. Releases ask GitHub for a green heavy run, not the tag.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    B1[PR: all jobs + advisory mutants]
    B2[push main: all jobs]
  end
  subgraph After
    A1[PR: affected packages incl. Windows and smoke]
    A2[push main: everything with no detection + mutants, coalesced]
    A3[nightly: same as push]
    A4[dispatch: optional module scope]
    A2 -->|green| T[move verified pointer]
    A3 -->|green| T
    A2 -->|real failure| I[open or update ready issue]
    A3 -->|real failure| I
    T -.-> R[release checks the run, not the tag]
  end
```

## Problem & Current Context
Assumes `main` is the integration branch.
- `.github/workflows/mutants.yml:3-5,40-41`: PR-only, `--in-diff`, `continue-on-error: true`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:16-166`: every job runs on every PR, Windows included.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:39-45`: the gate only requires the tag to be an ancestor of `main`.

Recorded decisions this updates (owner decision, 13 Nov 2026). The PR makes these edits:
- `AGENTS.md:139-143`: mutants still advise, now in the heavy tier on `main`, nightly and on dispatch, over the diff since `verified`; survivors go to the run summary.
- `DECISIONS.md:222-224` ("Mutation testing advises on the diff"): keep "advises" and the rejection of whole-workspace and Windows runs; replace "a PR's changed Rust" with "the Rust changed since the last verified commit, in the heavy tier".
- `DECISIONS.md:215-217` ("Releases wait for approval"): add "`verified` is only a pointer. A release checks the GitHub API for a successful heavy run on its commit and refuses otherwise."
- `AGENTS.md:103-120`, `DECISIONS.md:203-205`: unchanged; Windows and required names stay on PRs.
- `AGENTS.md:159-161`: add the `ready` and `ci-regression` labels beside `area:*`.

## Specification / Architectural Contract
**Fast tier** (`pull_request`): all `ci.yml` jobs and names stay, minus `mutants.yml`. New `.github/scripts/changed.sh BASE HEAD` runs as a step and prints affected units. Mapping: `crates/thalvi-server/**` means server; `crates/thalvi-desktop/**` means desktop and app (app depends on it); `crates/thalvi-app/src/**` means app; `crates/thalvi-app/ui/**` means desktop-ui and the app build; `web/**` means web; `speech/**` and `compose.yaml` mean speech; `.github/scripts/issue-refs*` means issues. Root manifests, lockfile, toolchain, `.cargo/`, `.node-version`, `deny.toml`, `.github/workflows/**` or any unmapped path runs everything. A script failure, shallow clone or empty diff also runs everything. Skipping happens inside steps, so required job names stay. deny and secrets always run.

**Heavy tier** (new `heavy.yml`: `push` to `main`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`): the fast jobs with no detection, plus `cargo mutants --in-diff` over `verified..HEAD`, never the whole workspace. Group `heavy-main`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. Survivors (exit code 2) go to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and do not fail the run or file an issue. Build or test errors and timeouts (other exit codes) fail it.

**Scoped dispatch:** input `scope` (crate or UI package, blank = all) narrows tests and mutants. Scoped runs never move the tag and carry `run-name` saying so.

**`verified` pointer:** last job `needs` all heavy jobs, blank scope, `main` only; moves forward only (`merge-base --is-ancestor`), `contents: write` on that job alone.

**Release:** in `release.yml` `gate`, replace the ancestor check. Query `repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/heavy.yml/runs?head_sha=SHA&status=success` and require a blank-scope run on `main`; refuse otherwise. The tag is ignored.

**Regression issue:** a `report` job on real heavy failure (never PRs), `permissions: issues: write, contents: read`. Using `gh` with the job token, find the open issue labelled `ci-regression`, then comment or create one. Body: `git log verified..SHA`, failed jobs, run URL. Labels `ready`, `ci-regression`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A web-only PR runs web and Windows steps only for what changed and no mutants; a `Cargo.lock` PR runs everything.
- [ ] Breaking `changed.sh` makes a PR run everything; two quick pushes to `main` give one heavy run.
- [ ] A one-crate `scope` dispatch runs only that crate and leaves `verified` alone.
- [ ] A forced surviving mutant appears in the summary and the run stays green; a forced test failure fails it.
- [ ] Green moves `verified`; red does not; a late older run never moves it back.
- [ ] A forced failure files exactly one `ready` issue with range and run link; a second updates it.
- [ ] `release.yml` refuses a `desktop-v*` tag on a commit without a green heavy run, even when `verified` points at it, and accepts one with a run (dry run via `workflow_dispatch`).
- [ ] Labels `ready` and `ci-regression` exist after the PR, created by it if missing.
- [ ] The listed doc edits are in the PR.

## Sub-issues / Related
- #407: lands first; PRs target `main`.
- cybrex/Bryti#164: same design for Bryti.

- blending over black or over nothing, so the background term vanishes;
- a scale of 1, so `/ scale` and `* scale` agree;
- a corner radius below half the shape, so the clamp never applies.

This list comes from 4 of the 8 shards; the remaining shards' survivors will be added as a comment.

|---|---|---|

### Desired outcome

Each existing overlay test pins the behaviour it names. Every survivor above is either caught by a strengthened test or recorded in `.cargo/mutants.toml` with a one-line reason why it's equivalent or not worth a test.

- [ ] The blend, blur, rounded, ticker, cancel-button, countdown-words, draft/card and `Module::draw` cases above are caught by strengthened existing tests, or by table rows added to them. That means one test per behaviour, not one per mutant.
- [ ] `fade_at`'s `>` / `>=` mutants are confirmed equivalent and recorded with that reason, or a test catches them.

candidates.body:
## Goal

Make the status overlay recover from a vanished or failed surface without frame-rate retries or blocked controls, and report an unrecoverable overlay failure where the user can see it.

## In Short

A closed Wayland surface no longer leaves the overlay logically visible but invisible. Failed show/present attempts back off even if statuses keep arriving, and Hide or Press do not wait behind a pending configure. Startup, drawing, protocol, and connection failures appear through the existing tray/Settings error path and clear after successful recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Show or present overlay] --> B{Surface usable?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Overlay visible; clear previous failure]
  B -->|Closed or failed| D[Mark not visible and report failure]
  D --> E[Backoff bounds every attempt, including new statuses]
  E --> F[Next eligible status recreates the surface]
  A --> G[Hide or Press arrives]
  G --> H[Handled promptly even while configure is pending]
```

## Problem & Current Context

Confirmed on current `main` at 55cca7ec:

- `host/linux/layer.rs` consumes only one queued configure, clears a closed surface, then returns `Ok(())` when no surface exists. `crates/thalvi-app/src/overlay.rs` treats that as visible, so later statuses call `present` rather than `show`. A queued `Ready` ahead of `Closed` further hides the closure.
- Failed show/present still schedules the next animation frame. Wayland `show` can wait one second for configure on the same loop that handles messages and presses.
- Thread-start, plan/open, painter/draw/show failures print only to stdout. Wayland and X event loops can end on connection loss without reporting it. X non-press events, including protocol errors, are discarded.

**Agent reproduction, 2026-11-13:** a temporary fake-surface case on unfixed 55cca7ec showed once, marked the surface vanished, then delivered the next status. `cargo test -p thalvi-app --lib a_vanished_surface_is_shown_again_on_the_next_status --locked` failed with actual calls `["show", "vanished"]` instead of `["show", "show"]`. No desktop or paid service was contacted.

This issue is about one outcome: a reliable overlay or a visible reason it is unavailable. Unrelated review findings are not silently absorbed into it.

## Specification / Architectural Contract

### Recovery and responsiveness

- A closed or vanished surface counts as not visible. Drain/coalesce queued configure states so `Ready` then `Closed` cannot hide the closure. The next eligible status creates and shows a fresh surface.
- A failed show or present marks the surface state unknown/not visible. Retry at most once per second, with the backoff bounding **all** attempts; a new status does not bypass it. Do not retry at animation frequency.
- Press and Hide handling must not sit behind a pending configure/show. With a fake clock and controlled pending configure, process each within **100 ms** of its message rather than the one-second configure timeout.
- Move pure configure handling into testable logic and narrow the `.cargo/mutants.toml` exclusion to code that genuinely needs a live compositor.

### Reporting

- Start, open, painter/draw, show/present, Wayland/X connection-loss, and X protocol failures use the existing persistent tray/Settings error path with a plain reason. If the overlay itself remains usable, a short headline may appear there; a broken overlay must not be the only reporting channel.
- A successful show/present after recovery clears or replaces the previous overlay failure. Repeated identical failures do not spam notices.
- Do not discard X `Event::Error` or leave a lost event-thread connection as a silent invisible state.
- Preserve non-activation and click-through behavior. Any platform-specific change is exercised on that platform.

### Explicitly out of scope

- The live-draft toggle defect is tracked independently.
- The Windows no-focus test gap belongs to the implementation's normal qualification, not a standalone test issue here.
- GNOME click-through/scale, display-change placement, resource leaks at exit, cancel-race nits, restyle fallback, stale comments, and countdown log noise require separate demonstrated reports; do not fix them in this issue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The vanished-surface reproduction passes, including `Ready` followed by `Closed`, and fails on the unfixed code. The next eligible status recreates the surface.
- [ ] Paused-clock tests prove failed show and present retry at most once per second even under repeated statuses, and a controlled pending configure does not delay Hide or Press beyond 100 ms.
- [ ] Fake-based tests prove start/open/draw and connection/protocol failures reach the user-visible error state, repeated failures do not spam, and successful recovery clears it.
- [ ] On the real Hyprland rig, closing the overlay surface or removing its output mid-capture recovers at the next eligible status; captured frames, state, and logs show the before/after behavior. Establish the close mechanism as part of the proof.
- [ ] Any changed GNOME or Windows platform path is exercised on that real desktop; the PR names every desktop used. No focus or click-through regression is introduced.
- [ ] Applicable Rust app/desktop tests, the server gate, and formal checks required by touched files pass. No paid service is called.

## Sub-issues / Related

- Follows #384/#242 and uses the existing error-presentation decision in `DECISIONS.md`.
- Supersedes the removed WebView overlay-command report #358.
- #423 tracks the separate live-draft toggle defect.

### Problem

The seven `spotter::tests` that use `network_fixture()` (`crates/thalvi-desktop/src/spotter.rs`) download the gigaspeech keyword-spotter files (encoder, decoder, joiner, bpe) from modelscope.cn into `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/tmp/models`, and `unwrap()` the result. Two things make `gates server` fail on code that has nothing to do with them:

- **Every fresh target dir downloads again.** That is every dev-job run on the developer machine. CI already caches `target/tmp/models` keyed on `models.rs`, so CI only downloads cold when that file changes.
- **Parallel tests stampede.** Each test calls the fixture itself, and `ModelStore::fetch` gives every caller its own `.part` file. A cold parallel run therefore starts up to 7 downloads of each file at once, about 28 connections to modelscope.cn.

Evidence:
- On 2026-11-10, 5 of 6 `gates server` runs failed this way on #342 and #350, and 3 of 4 on #362 (a server-only change). Each failed on a different subset of spotter tests, with `Download { kind: Spotter, … Connect, TimedOut }` at the 10 s connect timeout (`models.rs`).
- A single-threaded warm-up still had 2 of 13 time out.
- A one-off `curl` of the same files took 1.5 s.

So deduplicating within a run isn't enough on its own. The gate has to stop needing the network on every fresh target dir.

### Desired outcome

Decided in refinement:
- The spotter test models live in a per-user cache outside the target dir. A machine downloads them once, and again only when a model changes.
- Tests in one run share a single fetch per file.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `network_fixture()` uses a `ModelStore` at `dirs::cache_dir()/thalvi/test-models` (`~/.cache/thalvi/test-models`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\thalvi\test-models`), not under `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. It never touches the app's real store (`ModelStore::per_user`, `…/thalvi/models`). There is no env var or other override.
- [ ] The fixture fetches each file at most once per test process, through a shared `tokio::sync::OnceCell` (or equivalent), so parallel tests start one download per file. Concurrent processes stay safe, because `fetch` already writes to a per-process `.part` file and renames it into place.
- [ ] With the cache filled, the spotter tests make no network request: a fresh `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` passes with the network unplugged.
- [ ] A download failure still names the file and the host.
- [ ] CI's `actions/cache` steps in `ci.yml` (server, desktop-windows) and `mutants.yml` cache the new directory instead of `target/tmp/models`.
  - The cache key carries `runner.os`, since the path differs per OS, and drops `enableCrossOsArchive`.
  - It is still keyed on `crates/thalvi-desktop/src/models.rs`, and renamed from `wake-models` to what it holds.
- [ ] Nothing else reads `target/tmp/models`. If something does, it moves too, and no dead path is left behind.
- [ ] Used on the developer machine: two consecutive `gates server` dev-job runs with fresh target dirs, the second downloading nothing. Also `gates desktop-windows` on `windows-latest` CI.

### Context and related issues

- Supersedes #368 (same failure, closed as a duplicate; its evidence is folded in above).
- Seen during #342, #350 and #362 (PRs #371, #370).
- The workaround until this lands: run `cargo test -p thalvi-desktop --lib spotter::tests -- --test-threads=1` once in a reused dev-job session, then gate in that session.

## Goal

Cut the time agents spend repeating full local gates without reducing what CI checks. While editing, run the closest useful check; before pushing, run each affected component's gate once and leave routine AppImage/NSIS packaging to CI.

## In Short

Agents no longer run the whole workspace and a release package after every fix. A server-only change gets server tests while editing and the affected server gate before pushing; a desktop-UI change gets its UI checks, not an unrelated speech or web run. AppImage and NSIS builds run locally only when packaging itself changes.

PR CI keeps its current affected jobs and still packages app changes. The heavy `main` run still runs every gate and mutation testing. This issue changes local policy and documentation, not CI coverage, and it does not adopt nextest, sccache, or a new shared target directory.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Edit] --> B[Closest affected test or check]
  B --> C[Change is ready to push]
  C --> D[Select affected components from the diff]
  D --> E[Run each affected gate once]
  E --> F{Packaging or bundle inputs changed?}
  F -->|Yes| G[Build the affected package locally]
  F -->|No| H[Skip local package; PR CI still builds it]
  G --> I[Open PR]
  H --> I
  I --> J[Affected PR CI]
  J --> K[Heavy run on main: every gate plus mutants]
```

## Problem & Current Context

The documented local gate is `.github/scripts/gates <component>`, but there is no agreed distinction between an inner-loop check and a pre-push gate. Agents therefore repeat expensive full runs while iterating.

On current `main`:

- `gates server` installs and builds the desktop UI, then runs formatting, workspace clippy, tests, docs, and an AppImage release build. `gates desktop-windows` similarly ends in an NSIS build.
- The script already accepts `TESTS` to narrow Cargo packages and `BUNDLE=false` to skip packaging. PR CI uses both; local instructions do not say when to use them.
- `.github/scripts/changed BASE HEAD` already supplies the PR path mapping. An unreadable, empty, shallow, mixed-unknown, or otherwise unmapped diff deliberately falls back to `all`.
- #416 established the current CI contract: PRs run affected steps, required always-on checks remain, and `heavy.yml` runs everything on `main`, nightly, and on request.
- #421 already removed routine local mutation runs and made desktop verification reuse the change worktree's warm target. Those decisions stay in force; this issue does not reopen them.
- The earlier three-day dev-job sample (1,076 jobs, 303 failed, 57 cancelled, about 37 hours of build-slot time) is motivation, not a per-step baseline. The baseline still needs measured step times and rerun counts.

## Specification / Architectural Contract

### 1. Measure before changing the policy

Use retained dev-job records and logs first; do not run extra full gates merely to manufacture data.

- Record UI build, fmt, clippy, tests, docs, and AppImage time, warm and cold where the records distinguish them. State sample sizes and sources. Use heavy-CI records for mutation time per mutant; no new local mutation run is needed for this baseline.
- Count how often retained work reruns a full gate on the same PR. If a requested number is unavailable, say so rather than estimating it.
- Measure a representative server-only change before and after the staged policy. Report comparable wall-clock samples and their conditions, not only a theoretical sum of skipped steps.

### 2. Document three local stages

**Inner loop:** run the closest check that observes the edit: the affected Rust crate and test filter, or the affected UI/web test and static check. Do not run workspace tests, docs, mutation testing, or packaging at this stage.

**Before pushing:** after the changes are committed, use `.github/scripts/changed origin/main HEAD` to select components, then run `.github/scripts/gates <component>` once for each affected component.

- Reuse the existing `TESTS` narrowing for affected Rust crates. Do not create a second path-mapping implementation or a second inventory of gate commands.
- Set `BUNDLE=false` for ordinary source changes. Build an AppImage or NSIS package locally only when the diff changes Tauri configuration, bundle assets, installer/AppImage scripts, or packaging logic. An unmapped diff keeps the safe `all` fallback and does not disable packaging.
- A platform gate that cannot run locally remains explicitly unrun, not passed; Windows CI or a real Windows machine covers it.
- Existing pre-commit secret scanning and CI's always-on checks remain in place. Local staging never replaces a required CI result.

**After pushing:** PR CI remains the affected fast tier from #416. A green full heavy run on `main` remains the full-coverage backstop. No workflow, required-check, release-safeguard, or mutation-coverage change is part of this issue.

Mutation testing remains as #421 decided: locally only when an issue explicitly requests it, then with `--in-diff` against the base. Desktop verification keeps using the change worktree's warm target.

### 3. Implement only the policy and its evidence

Update `AGENTS.md`, the affected verification skills, and the relevant `DECISIONS.md` entry together. `.github/scripts/gates` remains the single source of component commands; `.github/scripts/changed` remains the single source of path selection.

Do not adopt nextest, sccache, a shared cross-worktree target, or another build tool in this issue. If the baseline identifies a remaining bottleneck, file a focused follow-up with that evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A linked baseline table reports the requested gate-step times, warm/cold conditions, sample sizes, and sources, plus the full-gate rerun frequency available from retained records. Missing data is stated explicitly; no new local mutation run is performed for the baseline.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md`, affected skills, and `DECISIONS.md` describe the same three stages, including the exact pre-push command

## Goal

"Open google.com" should open the site when the recognizer writes the host as words, like "Open Google dot com". Today Thalvi refuses it, or leaves it as dictation.

## Problem & Current Context

The on-device recognizer (Nemotron Streaming) writes "Open Google dot com". The `open <host>` matcher (`spoken_url`, `crates/thalvi-desktop/src/tasks.rs`) only accepts a literal dotted host such as `google.com`. That breaks two paths:

- **With an ending** ("…, do that"): `tasks::decide` returns `NotConfigured`, and the task is refused as not configured.
- **Without an ending** (#204, PR #270): `is_whole_task` (`crates/thalvi-desktop/src/capture.rs`) uses the same `tasks::decide`. The whole capture isn't recognized as a task, so it stays open as dictation.

Already settled by the code: the matcher only runs on text that starts with `open `, so dictated prose never turns into a URL. Every form accepted here also starts a task with no spoken ending, which is why the set of accepted forms stays narrow.

Found by the independent verifier for PR #270 on Hyprland, in the sandbox rig, with a synthesized voice and on-device Nemotron Streaming. The configured script phrases already arm correctly ("TASK IN 1 s"). The only gap is turning a host spoken as words into a host.

## Specification / Architectural Contract

In `spoken_url`, after the `open ` prefix and the trailing sentence punctuation are removed, a spoken host is rewritten before the existing validation runs:

- **Only "dot".** The whole word "dot", in any case, becomes `.`. "slash", "dash" and other spoken punctuation are out of scope; a later issue can add them if users ask.
- **Words within a label are joined.** Spaces between words before the last "dot" are removed: "stack overflow dot com" becomes `stackoverflow.com`, "Google dot co dot uk" becomes `google.co.uk`.
- **The part after the last "dot" is one word.** "example dot com extra" stays rejected, the same as the literal `open example.com extra` today.
- **The rewrite only applies when there is at least one "dot" word.** A literal host is handled as today, and spaces without a "dot" are still rejected.
- **The rewritten text goes through the existing checks unchanged:** dotted labels of letters, digits and hyphens; no credentials, port 0, bad percent-escapes or non-ASCII. "open dot com", "open Google dot" and "open dot" stay rejected.
- **The notice names the real host.** For a spoken form, the task label is the rewritten host, so the notice reads "Asked the browser to open google.com.", not "…Google dot com."
- **No change to** configured script phrases, Discord prefix matching, dictation text, or the silence-commit timing for tasks (DECISIONS.md "Silence commits capture").
- **No new decision bullet:** this extends the existing `open <host>` rule in "Two wake entries, endings select the capture route" without changing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] "Hey Thalvi, open Google dot com, do that" opens `https://google.com`, and the notice names `google.com`.
- [ ] "Hey Thalvi, open Google dot com" with no ending arms the task ("TASK IN …") and opens the site when the countdown ends, as `open google.com` does today.
- [ ] "open stack overflow dot com" opens `https://stackoverflow.com`; "open Google dot co dot uk" opens `https://google.co.uk`.
- [ ] These stay unmatched (`NotConfigured`, or dictation when there is no ending): "open example dot com extra", "open dot com", "open Google dot", "open Google slash maps", "open my site", plus every case `spoken_url` rejects today.
- [ ] The cases go into the existing table-driven `spoken_url`/`decide` test, not a new near-copy test; one `is_whole_task` case covers the no-ending path.
- [ ] `cargo mutants --in-diff` leaves no surviving mutant in the rewrite, or each survivor is judged equivalent in the PR.
- [ ] Qualification: in the sandbox rig, with a synthesized voice through the virtual microphone, using on-device Nemotron Streaming *and* Nemotron Unified, both phrases above open the site. The PR records the transcript each recognizer produced. Server recognizers are listed as not checked if they aren't run.

## Sub-issues / Related

- Related: #204 / PR #270 (whole-capture commands without an ending), where this was found.
- Related: #144 (personal vocabulary). That issue is about recognizing names; this one is about turning spoken punctuation into a host.

## Problem

Nothing runs fuzzing or long property tests, and Heavy runs mutants only on recently changed Rust in a few files. Running these for hours on the owner's main PC competes with training and interactive work.

## Change

`.github/scripts/break-it` has two commands (`--help`):

- **`break-it inside --hours H [--mutants] [--out DIR] [--no-install]`** runs in a Linux checkout.
  - **Setup:** installs whatever is missing: apt packages (with sudo), rustup, the pinned 1.99.0 and fuzz nightly toolchains, Node from `.node-version` (SHA-256 checked), `cargo-fuzz@0.13.2` and `cargo-mutants@27.1.0`. It builds the UI, the property-test binaries and the fuzz targets, so the time budget H covers only the stages.
  - **Property tests:** every test inside a `proptest!` block, found in the source, at `PROPTEST_CASES=1000000` with a random `PROPTEST_RNG_SEED`. One `cargo test` per test binary, in parallel, for about 15 % of H. They stop when done; nothing loops.
  - **Fuzzing:** every target in parallel, `-fork=nproc/targets`, ignoring crashes, timeouts and OOMs so it keeps going for the rest of H. Afterwards each failing input is replayed and grouped by crash site (panic location, sanitizer error, timeout or OOM). Three inputs per site are kept, with a symbolized `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` trace.
  - **Mutants, with `--mutants` only:** the whole workspace, using a temporary copy of `.cargo/mutants.toml` without `examine_globs`, so the recorded equivalent-mutant exclusions still apply. It runs with `--jobs nproc/8`, `--timeout 600` and Heavy's memory limit, stopped with SIGINT when its half of the time is up.
  - **Report:** `summary.md` gives the ref, commit, hours, cost estimate, and one row per stage with result, time and notes. A broken stage (`BROKEN` plus the error) reads differently from one that found bugs (`FAILED (n findings)`). Then the failing property tests with seed, last panic and shrunk input, and each fuzz crash site with an example input and the error. Exit 0: nothing found. 1: something found. 2: the run broke.
- **`break-it cloud --ref REF [--hours H] [--size xl|large|medium] [--mutants] [--out DIR] [--yes]`** runs `inside` on a Docker cloud sandbox.
  - **Before creating anything:** refuses H above 8 or not above 0, an unknown size, a ref that isn't a branch or tag on GitHub, and a local branch with commits GitHub lacks (a local branch that is only behind is fine). It prints the estimated cost and asks, unless `--yes`.
  - **The run:** creates one `shell` sandbox with `--ttl` = H + 1 h and `--on-timeout delete`, clones REF, and starts `inside` detached (`setsid`), so a dropped `exec` connection doesn't end it. It follows the log every 30 s and copies the report to `~/thalvi-break-it/<date>-<ref>-<short sha>/`.
  - **Cleanup:** an EXIT trap deletes the sandbox on every path, including Ctrl+C. No secrets enter the sandbox: it clones the public repo over HTTPS.
- **Checks:** `.github/scripts/break-it.test.sh` tests the refusals and the cleanup offline, with a fake `sbx` and a local bare repository. It runs in `gates issue-sync` with shellcheck.
- **Docs:** AGENTS.md says what break-it is, and that only a person, or an agent explicitly asked to, starts `break-it cloud`. `decisions/repository.md` has a bullet for the choice. `break-it-report/` is git-ignored.

## Platforms

n/a: no desktop app change. Linux only: `inside` ran on Ubuntu (x86_64) and in Debian 13 cloud sandboxes.

## Verification

| acceptance | result |
|---|---|
| `inside --hours 0.1` on a clean checkout under dev-job | Report folder with every stage listed. **Exited 1, not 0**: the property stage found a real bug on `main`, filed as #750. Every seed tried fails, so I couldn't show exit 0 on this checkout. |
| Planted failures (throwaway worktree, not committed: a `panic!` in `tasks_decide`, a property failing at 1 in 50,000 cases) | Exit 1. The summary names both, with seed 401088287 and inputs: the planted property shrunk to `n = 5563998309931250000` after 63,805 successes, and the fuzz panic showed as one crash site from 9,988 inputs. |
| A stage that can't run (`--no-install`, fuzz toolchain pinned to an uninstalled nightly) | Exit 2. The summary shows `fuzzing: BROKEN, the nightly-2026-11-01 toolchain failed: the nightly-2026-11-01 toolchain is not installed`. |
| `cloud` refuses an unpushed ref and `--hours 9` before creating anything | Refused, exit 2, `sbx --cloud ls` empty. The offline test also covers `--hours 0`, an unknown size, an unknown ref, an ahead branch, behind branches, tags, and cleanup after a failed clone. |
| Live: `cloud --hours 1 --yes` on xl | Report delivered to `~/thalvi-break-it/2026-11-27-test-break-it-run-c9b8961/`. Sandbox deleted (`sbx --cloud ls` empty). I used `--ref test/break-it-run`, not `main`: the sandbox runs the script from its clone, and `main` doesn't have it yet. The branch is `main` plus this script. |
| Live: Ctrl+C during fuzzing | SIGINT went to the process group a minute into fuzzing. Exit 130, `deleting break-it-20261127-015116`, and `sbx --cloud ls` listed only the other run's sandbox, itself deleted at its end. |
| Billing for the day | **Not checked**: the Docker billing page needs the owner's login. By the clock, about $1.25 (67 min on xl) plus about $0.20 for the Ctrl+C run and a short probe. |

Summary of the live run (the long assertion message is shortened):

```text
- ref: test/break-it-run
- commit: c9b8961d12ced9f7780173ef5dd5d60d3f26f12c
- hours: 1
- cost estimate: about $1.49 on xl
- started 2026-11-27T01:41:37Z, finished 2026-11-27T02:48:08Z
- exit: 1

| stage          | result             | time    | notes                           |
| setup          | passed             | 5m 59s  |                                 |
| property tests | FAILED (1 finding) | 1m 24s  | seed 3413373195, 1,000,000 cases|
| fuzzing        | FAILED (1 finding) | 59m 08s | 4 targets, -fork=4 each         |
| mutants        | skipped            |         | without --mutants

## Problem

The `cargo mutants` step in `.github/workflows/mutants.yml` runs with `continue-on-error: true`. That keeps surviving mutants advisory, as AGENTS.md intends, but it also hides runs that tested nothing:

- On #384 `ec3e2b3`, the unmutated baseline failed in all 8 shards (cargo-mutants exit 4), so no mutant ran. All 8 checks were green.
- On #384 `ce46e6a`, shards 2 and 4 hit the 60-minute step limit after about 49 and 78 of 127 mutants. Both were green.

A green shard therefore can't be told apart from one that tested everything and found nothing.

## Change

- The step keeps cargo-mutants' exit code. It passes for 0, 2 (missed mutants) and 3 (mutant timeouts), so survivors stay advisory. Any other code (4 for a failing baseline, 1 for a usage error, 70 for an internal error) fails the shard with a plain `::error::` line.
- `continue-on-error` is removed, so a step that hits `timeout-minutes: 60` now fails the job. The artifact upload still runs (`if: always()`).
- AGENTS.md says how to read the check: it's green with survivors, so count them from each shard's "M missed" log line. A shard that couldn't test fails.

The check stays advisory: it isn't a required check, so a red shard doesn't block a merge. It just no longer looks like a clean run.

## Platforms

n/a (CI only).

## Verification

- Ran cargo-mutants 27.1.0 on a throwaway crate: a missed mutant exits 2, a failing baseline exits 4. #392's CI logs show 3 for mutant timeouts.
- Extracted the edited step and ran it as GitHub does (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`) with a stub `cargo` exiting each code: 0, 2 and 3 pass; 4, 1 and 70 fail with the error line.
- The YAML parses, and the step no longer has `continue-on-error`.
- Not exercised: this PR changes no `*.rs`, so the mutants workflow doesn't run on it. The first Rust PR after it, or #384's next push once rebased, is the live check. The step-timeout failure relies on GitHub's documented `timeout-minutes` behaviour and wasn't triggered here.

## Problem

The heavy run's mutation testing has failed on `main` since the experimental Whisper helper landed, so `verified` has not moved. It fails in three ways:

- **Timeouts.** The `whisper.rs` tests wait up to 120 s for each event. A mutant that stops an event is caught only after minutes, or reported as a timeout, and shard 4 overran its 60-minute step.
- **Survivors.** 66 mutants in the code changed since `verified` were missed or never run.
- **A download that drops.** Shards 2, 3 and 6 of the latest run never built: ort-sys's ONNX Runtime download from cdn.pyke.io dropped.

## Change

- The Whisper test fakes answer within milliseconds, so test waits are now bounded at 5 s, the same as the other suites. Deadline tests drive tokio's paused clock instead of waiting it out. For that, `Shared::try_start` reads its readiness deadline from `tokio::time::Instant`, which is the same clock as std's unless a test pauses it.
- New or extended tests catch the survivors:
  - The Whisper helper as a real child process: its PID, last output, exit, kill and drop, and on Linux that it dies with the thread that started it.
  - The WAV header fields.
  - The loading steps and warm-up failures.
  - The model store's `stored` checks and the `source` of each listed speech model.
  - The final wait a chosen session gives.
  - How a `WindowApp` displays.
  - The limits GNOME reports.
- The rest go in `.cargo/mutants.toml`, each with a one-line reason:
  - Tauri commands that only pass `AppState` on, and `Runner::reload_speech_model`, added to the existing entries.
  - Two `Desktop::writing_target` arms: the Hyprland one needs a compositor, and the GNOME one equals the fallback.
  - Two equivalent Whisper mutants.
  - `whisper/windows.rs`, which only Windows compiles.
- The mutants job caches `~/.cache/ort.pyke.io`. ort-sys checks the download's hash and looks its binaries up by that hash, so a restored cache cannot hand it the wrong ones.

## Platforms

Windows locally: the `desktop-windows` gate's tests and lints. Hyprland and GNOME: CI only. The Linux-only tests (the helper dying with its thread, a file in place of the model folder, and GNOME's `recent_app`) could not compile here; they passed in this PR's CI and the heavy runs dispatched on this branch. No desktop session was used; the change is tests, one clock source and CI.

## Verification

- `main` was merged in at `3cbf316` (it had removed the server and web client and added the local chat model), and everything below was rerun on the merged tree.
- `.github/scripts/gates all` on Windows: the tests and lints passed. The packaging step stopped because `cmake` is not installed on this machine, so CI's `desktop-windows` job is the proof for packaging. `gates desktop-ui` passed.
- Formal source hashes match all three formal skills. gitleaks found nothing in the history. The commit messages and this title pass `.githooks/commit-msg`.
- The heavy run dispatched on this branch before the merge (`3f6a573`) passed every shard: 236 mutants caught, none missed, none timed out, and every CI gate including the Linux-only tests.
- The heavy run on the merged head `3cbf316` passed every shard and every CI gate: 327 mutants caught, none timed out. Its 56 missed mutants are all in code `main` added after this issue was filed (the local chat model from #505 and the terminal checks from #509); missed mutants only advise, and they are left for a follow-up.
- PR CI on `3f6a573` failed once on `app::tests::overlapping_saves_leave_the_file_and_the_running_config_agreeing`, which this branch does not touch; it passed on rerun. The test races: the start-at-login switch saves through `saves.remember`, which never records to `applied`, so `applied.last()` can lag the running config. It is on `main` too and is left for a follow-up.
- `cargo test -p thalvi-desktop --lib whisper` passed three runs in a row; the 43 tests now take about 1.4 s.
- Local `cargo mutants` runs (copy mode, a throwaway HOME, `--in-diff` against `verified`): all ten former timeouts are caught. Every listed survivor is caught except the ones excluded above; each exclusion regex was checked to match only its own mutant.
- An independent review found no proven defects. It raised that the parent-death check would fail on libtest's worker thread on Linux; that was fixed in `3f6a573` and re-reviewed with no findings.
- Not verified locally: Linux behaviour and the package build; CI covers both.

Closes #488

## Problem

Agents write both the code and the tests here, and several written rules have no check behind them:

- "Never commit secrets" relies on GitHub push protection, which only knows provider token formats. Generic patterns are off, so a key such as `LLM_API_KEY=...` gets through.
- Nothing watches Rust advisories. Dependabot only sends monthly version bumps, and its alerts and security updates are off for this repo.
- "Every behavior is tested" has no check at all.

## Change

Each tool was tried on this repo before deciding:

| Tool | Verdict | How it is added |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cargo-deny` 0.20.2 | Add, gate | `deny.toml` and a `dependencies` job: advisories, licences, sources |
| `gitleaks` 8.30.1 | Add, gate | `.gitleaks.toml`, `.githooks/pre-commit` and a `secrets` job over the full history |
| `cargo-mutants` 27.1.0 | Add, advisory only | `.cargo/mutants.toml` and `mutants.yml`: PR's changed Rust only, Linux only, survivors are annotations, never a failure |
| `proptest` 1.12 | Add, one test | One property on the Windows hold hook, the one place where event order is the rule |

`AGENTS.md` Gates and `DECISIONS.md` are updated here.

**New dependency:** `proptest`, dev-only, in `thalvi-desktop`, default features off. It adds 4 crates to the lockfile. Reason: the hold hook's rules must hold for any key order, the hook has needed two fixes for orders nobody had listed, and hand-written tables did not cover those orders.

**Repo settings, changed on the developer's go-ahead:** the `main` ruleset now also requires `dependencies`, `secrets`, `desktop-windows`, `desktop-ui` and `issues`, and Dependabot alerts are on. `mutants` stays out of the ruleset. A PR into `main` must contain these jobs for them to report, which this PR provides once it reaches `main`.

### Evidence

**cargo-deny**
- About 1s per run.
- With an empty config it reports 4 unmaintained advisories, all transitive (see Findings), and no vulnerabilities.
- It went red on an injected vulnerable crate and an injected GPL licence. A git dependency only warned by default, so `unknown-git = "deny"` is set, but I did not rerun the injection with that setting.
- It reads the lockfile for both targets, so it needs no Windows job. `windows*` crates and `zbus` both appear in its graph.

**gitleaks**
- 1s over all history (1,090 commits), 250ms on a staged change.
- One false positive, an empty `LLM_API_KEY= LLM_REASONING_EFFORT=`, handled by a one-line allowlist. No real secrets.
- It caught 8 of 10 synthetic secrets, including `LLM_API_KEY`, `STT_API_KEY`, a Baseten-style key, a Hugging Face token and a bearer header.
- It missed a Modal-style `ak-`/`as-` pair and a Meta-style `LLM|...|...` token, so it is a net, not a guarantee.
- Upstream says gitleaks is feature-complete and will only get security patches, with new work going to Betterleaks. Rules stay frozen, and swapping tools later would be a small change.

**cargo-mutants**
- The suites are stable: 5 of 5 repeat runs on all three crates, plus one-off server and app runs.
- Runs:

| Scope | Where | Mutants | Time | Missed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR #241 diff, before exclusions | Local, 4 jobs | 97 | 7m20s | 18 |
| PR #241 diff, with exclusions | GitHub runner, `--in-place` | 84 | 28m49s | 4 |
| PR #241 diff, with exclusions | GitHub runner, `--jobs 2` | 84 | 29m55s | 4 |
| Rule-heavy files | Local, 4 jobs | 293 | 18m11s | 20 |

- On a GitHub runner that is about 21s per mutant, so a whole-workspace run would take about 18 hours. Hence diff-only.
- It can't be a required gate: it can't tell a missing test from an equivalent mutant, and it doesn't see tests in other crates, so `Refusal::headline`, which `thalvi-app` uses, shows as missed.
- It doesn't run on Windows: that code has few host tests, and the shared logic is already mutated on Linux.

**proptest**
- 7 throwaway properties found 1 real gap (see Findings).
- The other 6 passed, including streaming chunk independence, and were dropped: they found nothing tables wouldn't.
- The committed property runs in about 0.02s and cuts `HoldHook` survivors from 7 to 2. It was a first attempt at 11 keys and 256 cases that missed most of them, so keys are now picked per hold key.

### Findings, reported and not fixed

**Possible bug**
- `crates/thalvi-desktop/src/hold.rs`: if the hold key's own release is lost, the hold never ends by itself. Modifier releases are reconciled for this (the code cites the lock screen), but the main key's aren't, so `Main::Swallowed` persists until that key is next pressed and released. The shrunk case is `F9` pressed, then released unseen, then any other key. Dictation keeps running, and that next press is swallowed. Found with the pure hook only; not reproduced on a real Windows desktop. For that reason the committed property does not cover lost releases.

**Test gaps (surviving mutants)**
- `capture.rs:515`: re-arming the same route with different text may inherit the old countdown. A second "submit" could be delivered sooner than its pause, on a route that reaches other people.
- `heard.rs:46`: the exact 50% boundary of the recorded heard guard is untested. `heard.rs:22` and `heard.rs:25` have edit-distance costs that are untested too.
- `capture.rs:599`: "scratch that" on an empty capture has no test. The committed property does not cover it; the throwaway capture property did.
- `capture.rs:679`: newlines inside `[artifact]` markers are untested.
- `boosting.rs:130` (fail-link token match) and `boosting.rs:175` (the bonus for tokens off the tree) are untested.
- `hold.rs:539`: the left Ctrl arm is not reliably reached by the property.

**Dependencies (no action needed now)**
- Unmaintained, transitive, no upgrade available: `proc-macro-error` (RUSTSEC-2024-0370, through `glib-macros`), `zbus_names`, `zvariant` and `zvariant_derive` (RUSTSEC-2026-0370 to 0372, through `zbus` in `tauri-plugin-single-instance`). `unmaintained = "workspace"` keeps these from failing the gate;

## Problem

Heavy CI on `main` could move the `verified` tag even when the randomized Settings exploration (`explore`) failed, because `verified` didn't depend on it. Mutation testing only advised: shards passed with surviving mutants, across every changed Rust file. So untested state, cancellation, delivery, hold-key and config-save code could land and be tagged verified.

## Change

- `.github/workflows/heavy.yml`: `verified` now needs `explore` and requires it to succeed, alongside `ci`, `mutants` and `gnome-appimage`. The `mutants` step passes only on cargo-mutants exit 0. Survivors (2), timeouts (3) and any other status fail the shard with a `::error::`, and the step summary lists the mutants.
- `.cargo/mutants.toml`: mutation testing is limited by `examine_globs` to six high-risk files:
  - `crates/thalvi-desktop/src/hold.rs`
  - `crates/thalvi-desktop/src/delivery.rs`
  - `crates/thalvi-desktop/src/engine.rs`
  - `crates/thalvi-desktop/src/engine/streaming.rs`
  - `crates/thalvi-app/src/settings.rs`
  - `crates/thalvi-app/src/runner.rs`
- Exclusions for files outside that list are gone. The remaining anchored `exclude_re` lines each carry a one-line proof that the mutant is equivalent or reachable only from native wiring.
- Tests that catch every mutant in those six files. Timeouts were fixed by bounding the waits that hung, so a broken build now fails its test instead of stalling the shard.
- Small production changes that keep behavior, where the code's shape made a mutant uncatchable:
  - `next_recorded` walks each join set once per poll, so no change to its cursor can spin synchronously.
  - `Engine::scan` spends cooperative budget each pass, so an always-ready key branch can't starve frames and timers.
  - The capture loop spends cooperative budget each pass, and waits for the Submit preview inline, so its branch is ready only when the overlay reports a change.
  - The quiet ending is taken before `on_quiet` handles it.
  - Stripping an extra's ending stops at an inferred ending.
  - `text_with_numbers` drops a check both callers already make.
  - `streaming_entries` is extracted from `DesktopRig::load`, so a test can drive it.
- `AGENTS.md` and `DECISIONS.md` describe the gating mutation step and the narrower scope.

Issue #642 (the intermittent `overlapping_saves` app test) is unchanged. It failed two local shard baselines under load, and those shards were rerun.

## Platforms

- Hyprland: the real app built from this head ran in the `verify-thalvi` sandbox (nested Hyprland, synthetic audio, on-device Nemotron). A hold dictation was delivered. A wake dictation had its spoken ending stripped. A wake task ended by a quiet pause ran after the pause. A live Submit showed its full-text preview through the countdown and was sent after the quiet pause.
- GNOME and Windows: not used. Windows is covered by CI only.

## Verification

- Mutation testing through the committed Heavy step, real cargo-mutants 27.1.0, eight round-robin shards:
  - all six files on `f06d87c3`: 980 candidates, 745 caught, 235 unviable, no survivors or timeouts;
  - everything changed in those files since then (the merge of `main` with #680, #681 and #683, and the capture-loop fixes), on this head: 60 candidates, 25 caught, 35 unviable, no survivors or timeouts.
- Assertion-removal control on `b0e9be6f` (`settings.rs` is unchanged since): deleting one `assert_eq!` in `settings.rs`'s key test let the `check_keys` `==` mutant survive, and the committed Heavy step exited 2 naming it. The intact tests caught it.
- `.github/scripts/gates formal` passed on this head:
  - capture-cancel: 242,147 distinct states, all invariants hold;
  - config-save: 131 states;
  - hold-keys harness: 351,684 real-code scenarios.
- `.github/scripts/gates all` on this head passed server (including the AppImage), desktop-ui, speech and issue-sync. The release gate stopped only because `minisign` isn't installed here; CI runs it.
- gitleaks passed on the full history. cargo-deny wasn't run locally. This PR changes no dependency files.
- An independent verifier checked:
  - the workflow wiring;
  - the Heavy step's exit handling, with a stub cargo for each status;
  - the six-file scope, with real `cargo mutants --list`;
  - the exclusion proofs. It refuted one, `EngineLink::quit`, which a test now catches. That exclusion was removed, and the mutant is proven caught through the Heavy step.
- A second independent check on this head confirmed the real-app cases above and the proofs of the two exclusions added since (`finish_runtime` and `quiet_allowed`).
- Not verified: a live Heavy run on GitHub. That runs after merge.

Closes #601

## Problem

The heavy run on `main` has failed since 9e7d66a, so `verified` cannot move. Two jobs fail:

- **`ci / dependencies`**: cargo-deny reports RUSTSEC-2026-0543. `chrono` is unmaintained, has no safe upgrade, and `thalvi-desktop` depends on it directly.
- **`mutants (1)`**: the shard ran out of its 60-minute step. cargo-mutants splits the mutant list into contiguous slices by default, so all 74 of shard 1's mutants are in `chat.rs` (the local chat model from #505). Most of them survive, and each survivor runs the whole test suite, so each takes about 60 s. The other shards finished in 28 to 55 minutes.

## Change

- `thalvi-desktop` uses `jiff` instead of `chrono`. `jiff` is the advisory's first recommended alternative.
  - Dictation folders are still named by local date and time (`2026-11-03/23-59-58`, `-2` for a repeat in the same second).
  - Copied error reports still say `Time: 2026-11-03 12:34:56 UTC`.
  - `time` was not used: it cannot read the local offset in a multithreaded Linux process.
  - `chrono` stays in `Cargo.lock` only through Tauri's `serde_with`. `deny.toml`'s `unmaintained = "workspace"` does not flag that.
- The heavy workflow's `cargo mutants` call shards round-robin. Over the diff since `verified`, each shard now gets 12 or 13 of the `chat.rs` mutants, out of about 75.

The `chat.rs` survivors themselves only advise, and #514 left them for a follow-up; this PR does not add tests for them.

## Platforms

Windows locally: the `desktop-windows` gate up to packaging, and a probe of `jiff`'s local time zone. Hyprland and GNOME: CI only. The app was not driven, because nothing visible changes: the two formatted strings are pinned by the existing tests, with their expected text unchanged.

Not verified:
- `jiff`'s local-zone lookup on Linux (`TZ`, then `/etc/localtime`). It is documented, but no Linux machine was available here.
- On Windows, `jiff` honours a `TZ` environment variable and `chrono` ignored it, so a user who sets `TZ` gets folder names in that zone. Windows never sets `TZ` itself.

## Verification

- `cargo deny --workspace --locked check advisories licenses sources`: passes on this branch and fails with RUSTSEC-2026-0543 on `main` at 9e7d66a.
- `.github/scripts/gates all` on Windows (that is, `desktop-windows`):
  - `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo lint` and `cargo test -p thalvi-desktop -p thalvi-app --locked` passed.
  - Packaging stopped because `cmake` is not installed here, so CI's `desktop-windows` job is the proof for packaging.
- Other gates run here:
  - `gates formal`, `gates desktop-ui` and the `formal-hold-keys` check passed.
  - The `formal-capture-cancel` and `formal-config-save` TLC checks found their covered sources unchanged. The model checks themselves did not run, because Java is not installed here.
- A `jiff` 0.2.39 probe on Windows resolved `W. Europe Standard Time` to `Europe/Berlin`, with the same local time and offset as the system clock.
- An independent review compared `chrono` and `jiff` output over 5.4 million instants. Everything from 1996 to 2045 matched, including every second around the daylight-saving changes. Earlier years differ because Windows applies today's EU rules to the past, while `jiff` uses the real history.
- `cargo mutants --list` over the diff since `verified` (596 mutants): the eight round-robin shards cover the list exactly once each, with 74 or 75 mutants per shard.
- Heavy run dispatched on this branch: https://github.com/NotPellew/Thalvi/actions/runs/44100214983. A branch run neither moves `verified` nor files an issue.
- gitleaks is not installed on this machine; CI's secrets check covers it.

## Problem

Writing fails with every self-hosted model that reasons before it answers. Qwen3 with its default chat template streams `reasoning_content` past the 15 s limit before any `content`. Thalvi read only `content`, so the user saw "Writing…" with nothing under it and then a generic "took longer than 15 seconds". The metrics showed `first_token_ms: null` and no sign the model had been thinking.

## Change

As decided on #335, the writing request is unchanged: strict endpoints answer an unknown field like `chat_template_kwargs` with 400. Thinking is shown to the user and explained instead.

- `writing.rs`: a streamed delta with nonempty `reasoning_content` (llama.cpp) or `reasoning` (newer vLLM and others) reads as `Piece::Thinking`. The type carries no text, so reasoning can never be shown or pasted. `content` wins when a delta carries both.
- Engine: new `EngineState::Thinking`, shown until the first text arrives. A timeout after reasoning and before any text is the new `WritingError::StillThinking`: "The writing model was still thinking after 15 seconds. Turn off its thinking on the model server. Nothing was pasted." The words go to the clipboard as with every writing failure. Cancel and the 15 s limit work as before.
- Metrics: `desktop_writing` adds `first_reasoning_ms` next to `first_token_ms`. Both count from the request start.
- App: `Status::Thinking`. Both overlay looks show "THINKING…" with the cancel button. The tray says "Thalvi: thinking", and the agent surface reports `writing`.
- README explains thinking models and `llama-server --reasoning-budget 0`. The `DECISIONS.md` entry on writing records the choice and rejects sending `enable_thinking`.

## Platforms

- [x] Hyprland 0.53.3 (sandbox rig, main PC, Ubuntu 26.04.1), PR head 15d0fc7, write dictations spoken into the rig microphone with `ctl write-start`/`write-end`. With Qwen3.5-9B (`llm-serve qwen3.5-9b`), the overlay showed THINKING… and, at 15 s, the still-thinking notice, with the words on the clipboard and nothing pasted. This held in both looks. Cancel while thinking pasted nothing and returned to listening. With Qwen3-8B (default template), 7 runs showed THINKING… then WRITING… and pasted. With Qwen3.5-9B plus `--reasoning-budget 0`, the text pasted after about 0.2 s. No reasoning text appeared in the overlay, paste, clipboard, logs or metrics. Results and metric lines are [in the PR comments](#issuecomment-6777125420).

Not verified: a physical write-key press (rig keys fire no binds), the tray menu, Windows and GNOME. Windows and GNOME share the changed code (engine, status, UI); no OS-specific code changed.

## Verification

- `.github/scripts/gates desktop-ui`: typecheck, lint, 247 tests, build. All passed.
- `server` gate steps `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo lint`, `cargo test --workspace --locked` (796 passed) and `cargo docs` all passed. The AppImage step was not run, since it always fails on this VM. Three spotter tests first failed because downloading their model from modelscope.cn timed out. They passed once the model was copied from a cached checkout.
- New and extended tests:
  - a table of SSE deltas → thinking or text
  - streamed thinking → `Thinking` state, then text, with only the text pasted
  - timeout while thinking → `StillThinking`
  - cancel while thinking pastes nothing
  - `first_reasoning_ms` and `first_token_ms` recorded separately
  - status, tray, overlay, agent and Settings tables gain the new state
- `cargo mutants --in-diff`: 27 mutants; 16 caught, 9 unviable and 1 timeout (counts as caught). One was missed: a redundant `first.reasoning.is_none()` check, which the second commit removes, since `set_state` already ignores a repeated state. CI's `mutants` job then ran `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` on 15d0fc7: 26 mutants, 17 caught, 9 unviable, 0 missed.
- `formal-capture-cancel` reported source drift for `engine.rs` (this PR) and `runner.rs` (#337). Neither touches a mapped await or control drain, so the hashes and the Covers note were refreshed. The full TLC check (15,896 states), the self-test and the real-code replay pass.

Closes #335

## Problem

With several second passes switched on, the paste waited for every one of them, even though only the first usable answer in list order is pasted. A slow or unreachable server whose text is only recorded delayed dictation by up to its 10-second timeout.

## Change

- Start all requests together and paste once the earliest usable entry in list order is known; fall through failed, timed-out or disagreeing entries and use live text if none is usable.
- Run recorded-only requests in tasks that measure their own latency and record their eventual text and metric. A recorded-only failure has its own notice.
- Cancelling the current wait cancels and records its requests; cancelling a later capture leaves recorded-only requests alone, and quitting stops them.
- Update the second-pass documentation and cancellation-model source mapping.

## Platforms

Used live on Linux Hyprland in an isolated nested compositor with the real desktop debug build, private PipeWire microphone, synthetic Piper speech, `wtype` hold key and a victim window. Scripted loopback ASR endpoints supplied the live transcript and the fast and delayed second passes. This does not exercise a physical microphone, physical keyboard, real ASR service or another desktop. Windows desktop use remains unverified here.

## Verification

- Merged `origin/development` (including #323's TLC v1.7.4 pin) into the branch without rebasing. Refreshed the cancellation model's sync commit to the inspected merge: `check.py` PASS (15,896 distinct states), `--self-test` PASS. Evidence: `/var/tmp/thalvi-formal-ntq0x68t` and `/var/tmp/thalvi-formal-0z__8_86`.
- Linux live comparison: clean development `261bb2e` **4,930 ms**, PR **973 ms** from the release bind's timestamp to the victim file's paste, with the same synthetic speech and scripted endpoints. Both pasted `Fast pasted words`. On the PR, `Slow recorded words` appeared in the capture text after paste and its metric reported 4,181 ms, `used: false`. The slow endpoint delayed its response by 4 seconds. Evidence: `/var/tmp/thalvi-rig/run-erAHzy/out/` (including `base-evidence/`, `pr-evidence/`, and isolation proof). These are observed end-to-end rig timings, not production ASR latency.
- Linux Rust gates: desktop UI `npm ci` and build, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo lint`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, and `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo docs` passed. The first test attempts hit an overlong temporary socket path and public model-download timeouts; the passing run used a short private `TMPDIR` and locally cached model fixtures. AppImage compilation succeeded but bundling failed at `failed to run linuxdeploy`; CI covers the bundle. Managed logs: `/home/yannic/.local/state/dev-job/jobs/20261109T205810-pr320-verification-67ffe7b3ea52/artifacts/`.
- Author's paused-clock engine tests cover list order, fall-through, cancellation, delayed recording and per-request timing. Author's diff mutation run: 26 mutants, 13 caught, 9 unviable, 4 timeouts, 0 missed. These are retained as prior results, not rerun in this verification.

Closes #316

## Problem

The mutation run on `main` fails its briefing shards (#429). One mutant survives: `is_briefing_tool` returning `true`, because no test sends a history search or an unknown tool call to a conversation that has a briefing source. Five others time out instead of failing: the source-timeout test pauses tokio's clock, and `wait_until` kept yielding without ever letting that clock reach its 5 s bound, so any mutant that kept the call from reaching the source spun forever.

## Change

`wait_until` now checks the wall clock, so a condition that never holds fails after 5 s even with a paused clock. A new test sends a history search and an unknown tool to a conversation with a briefing source and checks their task steps and that the source is never asked.

## Platforms

n/a (server tests only)

## Verification

## Problem

The heavy run on `main` fails every time on one mutant: `replace note_disconnect with ()` at `session.rs:2565` times out instead of being caught.

With `note_disconnect` doing nothing, the recognizer reconnects every 100 ms and sends `Ready` each time. `private_disconnect_and_reconnect_keep_provider_text_out_of_every_recording` gave each `recv` its own 5 s timeout, so under the paused clock every `Ready` renewed it, the loop never ended, and the test hung rather than failed.

## Change

The test waits for each expected `Disconnected` under one 5 s deadline for the whole wait. A recognizer that reconnects forever without reporting a loss now fails the test, so the mutant is caught.

The takeover model's `source.json` hash for `session.rs` is resynced; the diff is inside the test module and touches none of the covered functions.

## Platforms

n/a

## Verification

- `cargo mutants --in-place --package thalvi-server -F 'session.rs:2565:5: replace note_disconnect with'`: before the change `TIMEOUT` (test run hung past 60 s, 107 of 108 tests finished); after it, `caught`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p thalvi-server --all-targets --locked -- --deny warnings`, `cargo test -p thalvi-server --locked` (108 unit tests plus the integration tests) and `cargo doc -p thalvi-server` with `-D warnings`: all pass.
- `.github/scripts/gates formal`: passes.
- Not run: the full `gates server`. This VM has no `pkg-config` or GTK/WebKit libraries, so `cargo lint` stops on the desktop crates. CI covers that.
- Not run: the full heavy tier; the next run on `main` shows whether the other shards stay green.

## Problem

When a hands-free capture heard the user's words but missed their ending (say "… pace that" instead of "paste that"), it failed after a minute with the headline "No words heard" and "No words heard for 1 minute." The words had been heard and went to the clipboard; only the ending was missed. The user read it as a broken microphone or recognizer.

## Change

The idle timeout now looks at what the capture kept. If words were kept, it fails as "No ending heard: Didn't hear an ending for 1 minute.", and delivery adds its usual "Captured text is on the clipboard." If no words were heard at all, it still says "No words heard". Both paths that raise the idle timeout (the engine's idle step and the stalled-recognizer `feed`) use the same choice. The metrics outcome stays `no_ending`.

The engine message does not mention the clipboard itself: delivery appends that sentence only when the copy succeeded, and switches to "Clipboard failed — text in Settings" when it did not.

## Platforms

Hyprland (sandboxed nested rig, real app with the private microphone and on-device Nemotron): independent verifier. GNOME and Windows: not used; shared engine code.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt`, `cargo lint`, `cargo test -p thalvi-desktop` green. Three engine tests (idle step, configured limits, stalled `feed`) fail when the choice always returns `NoWords`.
- `cargo mutants --in-diff`: 7 mutants, 5 caught, 2 unviable, 0 missed.
- `formal-capture-cancel`: the change only picks which error is raised; source hash refreshed. The check passes (15,896 states), and so do `--self-test` and `repro.py`.
- Workspace gates on d44a3ea: `cargo fmt`, `cargo lint`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo docs` green.
- Independent verifier (GPT-6.1 Terra) in the sandboxed Hyprland rig, idle limit set to 10 s:
  - Missed ending ("… pace that"): the overlay shows "No ending heard" and the recording says "Didn't hear an ending for 10 seconds." The log adds "Captured text is on the clipboard.", the clipboard holds the sentence, and the metric is `no_ending`.
  - Silence after the wake word: "No words heard" / "No words heard for 10 seconds."
  - A normal "paste that" still delivers.
  - The formal check reruns green.
- Not verified: the full notice text on screen (the overlay frame shows the headline; the message was read from the log). A long clip lost its start in the rig, which is the known rig issue #297.

Closes #295

## Problem

Every recognizer gets different words wrong, but a second pass could only replace the live text, and the first ticked one in list order that answered won. No combination of recognizers could beat the best single one, and the list order was a ranking the user had to manage (#228).

## Change

The live recognizer works as before and decides the ending and route. Second passes become **extras**: with one or more switched on, the engine uploads the capture to each, then asks the writing chat endpoint (same `url`, `model`, key; its own fixed merge prompt) to merge the live text and the extras' texts into one. The merged text is pasted only if every word appears in an input. Fewer than two texts, a failed extra or chat call, the deadline, or an unfaithful (or wordless) merge pastes the live text, and the overlay says why. The route comes from the live transcript and is never re-parsed from the merged text. The overlay, tray and agent show a "Merging" step; cancel works during it. "Write that out" writes the merged text (a second chat call).

- **Stored shape:** entries of kind `extra` (same fields as `second_pass`). An old `second_pass` entry, and the old `stt.secondary` setting, load as extras and are written as `extra` on the next save. List order means nothing.
- **Chat endpoint rule:** an extra can be switched on only while `writing` is set. The loader refuses a hand-edited file in that state with the plain reason. `settings check/set` and the Settings window refuse switching one on without it, and refuse removing `writing` while one is on, each naming what to do first. Note: an existing file with a second pass **on** and no writing endpoint is now refused at start until one is set or the extra is switched off.
- **Deadline (decision, not measured):** 8 s from the end of the capture for extras and merge together; extras are waited for up to 5 s, the rest is for the chat call. Extras that miss the cutoff are left out and still recorded. A slow extra therefore delays the paste by up to 5 s. These are starting values, to be set from the measurements below.
- **Metrics/recordings:** `desktop_secondary_stt` is now `desktop_extra_stt`; new `desktop_merge` has the added latency (`duration_ms`), the chat call's own latency (`chat_ms`) and the outcome `merged | unfaithful | timeout | error | too_few` (and `cancelled`). `text.txt` has each extra's name and text and the merged text.
- **Removed:** the list-order fall-through and the recorded-only notices of #320; the arrows in Settings. README and DECISIONS are updated as the issue specifies. Not done, as out of scope: renaming `secondary.rs` (it also serves the OpenAI live entry) and an all-texts-agree shortcut that would skip the chat call (worth measuring first).
- `formal-capture-cancel`: the cancel model is unchanged (`Engine::merge` is the old `secondary` stage under a new name; both awaits poll cancellation first); notes and hashes updated and rechecked, and `formal-config-save` hashes and note likewise.

## Platforms

Desktop app change. **Not used on any desktop.** The agent machine has no Hyprland, GNOME or Windows session, so the real-app check from the issue (one capture merged and pasted, one skipped with the notice, with the measured added latency) is **not done**.

## Verification

Ran on the merged tree (with `origin/main` merged in): `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo lint`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo docs` with `-D warnings`, `gates desktop-ui` (typecheck, lint, 228 tests, build), `gates formal`, `formal-capture-cancel/check.py` (22,275 states, no error) and `formal-config-save/check.py`, gitleaks on the new commits. Engine tests use fake recognizers, a fake chat endpoint and a paused clock for: merge delivered; unfaithful, wordless, failed, empty and slow merge; failed, disagreeing and late extras; route and ending phrase kept; cancel at both awaits; both latencies recorded apart; write after merge; holds. Config and Settings tests cover the refusals and old files. No test calls a paid service. An independent review (GPT-6.1 Sol) found two bugs, both fixed with tests that fail without the fix: cancel dropped answered extras' records, and a punctuation-only merge replaced the words.

**Not verified:** the word-error-rate comparison on the developer's English/German/Spanish recordings, the measured added latency p50/p95 (and so the 8 s / 5 s values), and use in the real app on Hyprland. Cargo mutants was not run.

Closes #228
