candidates.body:
## Problem

Every Rust PR runs every CI job, Windows included, plus eight advisory mutants shards. PRs wait for all of that, and survivors appear only as capped annotations. Releases check only that the tag is on `main`.

## Change

This PR implements #406, now that `main` is the only integration branch (#408, #418).

- **Fast tier (`ci.yml`, `pull_request`):**
  - A new `changes` job runs `.github/scripts/changed BASE HEAD`. The script maps changed paths to units as #406 specifies. An unmapped path, a shallow clone, an unreadable diff or an empty diff gives `all`, and so does a failure of the script itself, with a warning.
  - Every job keeps its name. A job skips its steps when no change affects it, and says so in its log.
  - The server and Windows gates narrow `cargo test` to the affected crates (`TESTS`) and skip the package build when the app is unchanged (`BUNDLE=false`). Run locally, `gates` still does everything.
  - `deny`, `secrets`, `formal` and `release` always run.
  - A failed `changes` job leaves its outputs empty, and the jobs read empty as "run". A detection failure can never skip work.
- **Heavy tier (new `heavy.yml`; push to `main`, nightly, `workflow_dispatch`):**
  - It calls `ci.yml` with no detection, so it runs the same jobs and saves the caches on `main`. It also runs the 8 mutants shards over `--in-diff` of the Rust changed since `verified`.
  - Mutants exit codes 0 and 2 pass. Missed and timed-out mutants are listed per shard in the step summary; timeouts (3) and any other exit code fail the shard.
  - Group `heavy-<ref>-<scope>`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. A push run whose commit is no longer the head of `main` skips itself, so a burst of pushes gives one run. If the head of `main` can't be read, `start` fails instead of skipping.
  - A `verified` tag that isn't an ancestor of the run's commit fails `start` with an error; only a missing tag falls back to the parent range.
- **Scoped dispatch:** a `scope` choice (a crate, `web`, `desktop-ui`, or the default `all`) narrows tests and mutants. Scoped runs carry a `run-name` that says so and never move `verified` or file an issue.
- **`verified`:**
  - The `verified` job runs only after a fully green, unscoped run on `main`. It alone has `contents: write`.
  - It moves the tag only forward (`merge-base --is-ancestor`), fails if it can't read the tag, and pushes with `--force-with-lease` on the value it read, so a concurrent move is never overwritten.
  - **Bootstrap:** with no `verified` tag, the first run tests the commits since its own parent, i.e. the change that just landed, then creates the tag. This needs no manual step.
- **`report`:** on a real failure on `main` (never on a scoped run, a PR or a cancellation), it comments on the open `ci-regression` issue, or opens one labelled `ready` and `ci-regression`. The body has the run URL, the failed jobs and `git log` since `verified`. It uses the job token with `issues: write` on this repo only.
- **Release (`release.yml` gate):**
  - A `desktop-vX.Y.Z` tag needs a successful `heavy.yml` run on its commit on `main` whose `verified` job succeeded. Only full green runs have one, so scoped and superseded runs don't count, and the tag is ignored.
  - Development builds keep only the on-`main` check, as the coordinator decided.
- `mutants.yml` is deleted. `.cargo/mutants.toml` is unchanged.
- **Docs:** the AGENTS.md mutants paragraph and labels line, DECISIONS.md's mutants and releases bullets as #406 specifies, a new "PRs run what changed" bullet, and the cache bullet now names the heavy tier.

## Platforms

n/a (CI only). The Windows job and the Windows smoke ran on GitHub's `windows-latest` in the runs below.

## Verification

All of this was run for real on GitHub, using throwaway PRs and a throwaway branch `test/heavy-dryrun`. That branch carried a copy of `heavy.yml` with three substitutions: its own branch for `main`, the tag `verified-dryrun`, and the labels `ready-dryrun` and `ci-regression-dryrun`. Everything else ran unchanged.

| #406 acceptance criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| A web-only PR runs web and Windows steps only for what changed, with no mutants | Live, throwaway #410: `web` ran; the other jobs, Windows and smoke included, skipped their steps within seconds and reported green |
| A `Cargo.lock` PR runs everything | Live, #411: units `all`, `cargo test --workspace`, every job ran |
| A desktop-UI PR runs desktop-ui and the app build | Live, #412: units `desktop-ui`; AppImage, NSIS and smoke ran, with "SKIPPED cargo test"; web, speech and issues skipped |
| Breaking `changed` makes a PR run everything | Live, #413: "changed failed, so everything runs" and units `all`; `issues` went red because it tests the broken script |
| Two quick pushes give one heavy run | Live: of two pushes seconds apart, the first run logged "A newer push … will test this commit too" and skipped; the second ran in full. A push that lands after the first run's `start` job still gets its own run, queued behind it |
| A one-crate `scope` dispatch runs only that crate and leaves `verified` alone | **Not run live:** dispatch needs `heavy.yml` on the default branch. Covered by reading the code only; to run after merge |
| A surviving mutant appears in the summary and the run stays green | Live: an untested function's 4 mutants were MISSED, each shard summary listed them ("### Shard 0: 1 missed …"), and the run was green |
| A forced test failure fails the run | Live: a failing `judge` test turned `ci / server` red, mutants shards with mutants to test failed with "cargo mutants exited with 4", `verified` was skipped, and #415 got a comment. (An earlier attempt failed on `cargo fmt` first; that also turned the run red) |
| Green moves `verified`; red does not; a late older run never moves it back | Live: green moved the dry-run tag a8ef508 → 95b0772; red runs left it there; re-running the older run's `verified` job logged "verified is at 95b0772…, which is newer…, so it stays"

## Problem

Thalvi's own instructions make machines do avoidable heavy work: `AGENTS.md` reads as an order to run `cargo mutants` locally (250 runs wrote 577 GiB in 4.5 hours on 12–13 Nov), the desktop verification recipe does a fresh `npm ci` plus a cold cargo build in a `dev-job` scratch that only one machine has, and `formal-capture-cancel` leaves a `/var/tmp/thalvi-formal-*` folder after every run.

## Change

- `AGENTS.md`: mutation testing runs locally only when the issue explicitly asks, and then only `--in-diff` against the base. `DECISIONS.md` records the 13 Nov owner decision in the existing mutation entry.
- `verify-thalvi/desktop.md`: build in the change's own worktree and keep its `target/`; skip the UI build when no source is newer than `ui/dist` (Tauri embeds `dist`, so rebuilding identical files would recompile the app); no `dev-job`. Machine build rules apply when the run's brief carries them.
- `formal-capture-cancel/scripts/check.py`: a passing run deletes its evidence folder. A counterexample, a blocked run, and `--self-test` keep it and print `EVIDENCE=…`. The PASS line no longer prints a path to a deleted file. SKILL.md updated to match.

## Platforms

n/a (skills and docs only). The desktop rig was not run: this machine has no desktop rig or webkit headers.

## Verification

- `check.py` on the passing model: `/var/tmp/thalvi-formal-*` count 13 → 13, exit 0.
- `check.py --self-test`: `SELF-TEST PASS`, folder kept and `EVIDENCE=` printed (count +1).
- A copy of the skill with `DropCompletionGuard = TRUE`: `FAIL`, exit 1, folder kept and printed.
- `grep -rn dev-job .agents/skills/verify-thalvi`: no matches.
- Desktop UI step, run three times in this worktree: first `BUILD`, second `SKIP`, `BUILD` again after touching a UI source.
- `.github/scripts/gates formal` passes; `bash -n` on `thalvi-verify` passes.
- Not verified: the `cargo build -p thalvi-app` step and the copy to `/var/tmp/thalvi-rig/bin/`, which need webkit and a desktop rig. A second `cargo build` of an unchanged tree is cargo's own no-op.

Closes #414

## Problem

The suite had grown near-copies, tests that were subsets of later broader tests, and tests that never ran:
- shell, PowerShell and Python test scripts nothing called;
- the real whisper helper tests, which passed without their inputs;
- the sandboxed socket test, which printed "skipped" and passed when user namespaces were missing. Ubuntu's AppArmor blocks those namespaces by default, so CI may have been passing it without running it.

Nothing stopped new ones, and the AGENTS.md rule "A bug fix adds a test that fails without it" pushed toward new test functions over extending existing ones.

## Change

- **Clear duplicates (Rust and the settings UI):** merged near-copies into table rows and deleted tests whose checks a broader test already makes. Rust went from 1,104 to about 970 tests, before the merge of main removed the extra-recognizer tests.
- **Unsure cuts:** settled with cargo-mutants, run only on the functions behind them.
  - 31 more tests removed, because no mutant survives without them.
  - 11 kept: 6 each catch a mutant nothing else does, and 5 can't be merged within clippy's line limit or share no setup.
- **Unrun tests:**
  - deleted the four test scripts nothing ran (`e2e/gnome/check.test.sh`, `e2e/windows/transcript.test.ps1`, `verify-thalvi/scripts/thalvi-desktop-rig.test.sh`, `speech/asr/test_nemo_stream.py`);
  - the real whisper helper tests are `#[ignore = "<how to run them>"]` and fail when their inputs are missing;
  - the sandboxed socket test fails instead of skipping, and the CI jobs that run the desktop tests (server, Heavy mutants) enable unprivileged user namespaces first.
- **New check:** `.github/scripts/test-hygiene` (in the server gate) fails on three things:
  - a test script that no runner names;
  - a Rust test that returns early instead of being ignored;
  - two Rust or TypeScript tests with the same body.
- **Flaky test fixed:** the stale-socket check now shuts its listener down before dropping it. A child process another test forks in that window holds a copy of the listener, which kept the "stale" socket accepting connections under load.
- **AGENTS.md:** a fix or feature first extends the existing test of that behavior and adds a test only when none covers it.
- **Housekeeping:**
  - dropped the `redundant_clone` lint budget no exception uses;
  - refreshed the formal source hashes. Every edit to a covered file is inside its test module.

## Platforms

n/a for app behavior: only tests, CI and docs change. The Windows test edits were checked with `cargo xwin clippy` only; `gates desktop-windows` was not run.

## Verification

- **Gates after merging main:** `gates server` with the AppImage, `desktop-ui`, `speech`, `issue-sync` and `formal` all pass. `release` was not run: `minisign` isn't installed on this machine.
- **Sandboxed socket test:**
  - fails with its fix in the message when `unshare` is missing and when namespaces are refused;
  - breaking the sandboxed client's expected answer fails it, so the sandboxed child really runs.
- **Stale-socket fix:** a probe showed a forked fd holder keeps a dropped listener accepting connections, and that `shutdown` makes it refuse. The original failure didn't recur in 200 single runs or 15 full-suite runs.
- **Mutation runs:** cargo-mutants 27.1.0 in copy mode, with a throwaway `HOME` and no desktop session, on the functions behind the unsure tests. Every survivor was re-checked against the full suite.
- **Not verified:**
  - that the user-namespace step works on GitHub's runners; this PR's CI shows it;
  - the formal models weren't re-run in TLC, since only their source hashes moved.

candidates.body:
## Problem

The developer's workplace hosts whisper-large-v3, and colleagues with slow laptops want to dictate through it. That server takes the recording only on `/v1/chat/completions` as `input_audio`. It has no `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, which is the only request the OpenAI-compatible live entry from #385 could send. Whisper also guesses the language when it isn't given one, and on short dictations it sometimes guesses wrong.

## Change

The OpenAI-compatible live entry in Settings → Speech gets two settings.

**Request**
- **Transcriptions** stays the default and keeps today's request.
- **Chat with audio** sends one non-streaming `POST {address}/chat/completions` with `{"model": …, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": <base64 WAV>, "format": "wav"}}]}]}`.
  - The WAV is the same one the transcriptions upload sends.
  - The text comes from `choices[0].message.content`.
  - The 10 s deadline, the Bearer key and the failure messages work as in Transcriptions mode.

**Language**
- Optional; it must be an assigned ISO 639-1 code, in any case, such as `de`.
- Settings checks it where it's entered and refuses an unknown code such as `zz` or `deu` in plain words.
- When set, it's sent as `language`: a form field in Transcriptions mode, a top-level JSON field in Chat mode. When empty, nothing is sent and the server detects the language.

**Other changes**
- Saved configs without these fields load as Transcriptions with no language.
- The second-pass entry and the old `stt.secondary` format are unchanged.
- The `desktop_live_stt` metric now records `request: "chat" | "transcriptions"` with each request's latency and outcome.
- README and the DECISIONS.md recognizer bullet describe the new settings.
- `base64` (already a workspace dependency, used by the server) is now a dependency of `thalvi-desktop` too.

Out of scope, as #419 says: streaming in Chat mode, vocabulary hints, the second-pass entry, and the 10 s deadline.

## Platforms

- **Hyprland:** used in the sandboxed nested-Hyprland rig (`verify-thalvi`'s `desktop.md`), on the debug build of ec7dbc11.
  - The later commits only narrow language validation (unit-tested), move a formal hash, and bound a test wait.
  - Chat mode ran against a local fake chat-audio server that answers like the workplace server's documentation.
  - Transcriptions mode with a language ran against a real speaches 0.8.3-cpu on Cybrex2.
- **GNOME, Windows:** not used. CI builds and tests Windows.

## Problem

Thalvi Desktop has no way to update itself. Updating means downloading a new package by hand. The developer and colleagues testing development builds need new builds to arrive without that step.

## Change

Thalvi follows the update channel picked on the Settings **App** page: **Stable** (the default) or **Development**. It checks about 10 s after it is usable, then at most once a day; **Check for updates** checks now, joining a check already running. It downloads and verifies the update in the background through `tauri-plugin-updater`, using the signed, version-bound feeds of #346 and #388. It installs and restarts only when the engine thread itself finds Thalvi idle: no capture with its countdown, delivery or task, no held hold key, no fed clip. Until then the update waits.

- **Restart:** a one-shot `update.json` marker keeps the paused state across the restart, so a paused microphone stays closed. It also tells the next start what happened: "Updated to X", once, on the tray and in Settings, without opening or focusing a window. If the version didn't change, it shows what failed and the reinstall path instead.
- **Windows:** the per-user NSIS installer runs quiet (`/S /UPDATE /R`) and relaunches Thalvi in the user's session.
- **Linux:** the AppImage is replaced in place, then Thalvi restarts.
- **Versions:** Stable refuses a prerelease feed. Only a newer version installs, so switching Development → Stable stays on the development build until a newer stable release; the App page says so.
- **Unsupported installs:** an AppImage-less Linux run or an unwritable AppImage folder explains how to install from the release page, with no network request.
- **Failures:** a failed check, download, signature or install shows a plain error and leaves the installed version working; Retry checks again.
- **Metrics:** each check, download and install records outcome and latency in the opt-in metrics (`desktop_update`, versions and channel only).
- **Dependencies:** `tauri-plugin-updater` is Tauri's own updater, used for signature and version checks and the platform installers; `semver` was already in the tree through it.
- **Docs:** README "Updates" and the DECISIONS "Packaged desktop…" bullet. The capture-cancel formal model gains the restart request, which never ends a capture.

The real-use check found that the start after an update read Cargo's version, which lacks the `-dev.N` a development build gets at build time. A development update said "Updated to 0.1.5" for 0.1.5-dev.8, and a failed install between two development builds would have looked done. The start now uses the version the updater compares with (`fix(desktop)` commit).

## Platforms

Used for real on **Windows 11** (the laptop, per-user install as the non-admin user t3-agent) and **Hyprland** (the verify-thalvi rig, a real AppImage run through `APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN`). The updates came from a controlled feed: the throwaway public repository NotPellew/thalvi-release-trial, with this branch plus a commit that swaps in a throwaway key and the trial feed URLs, published by the #388 workflow. GNOME was not tried (#101).

- **Windows:**
  - Trial 0.1.3 installed by hand over the released 0.1.2. Paused, it updated itself quietly to 0.1.4 about 21 s after starting and came back paused, with one process in the user's session.
  - Its config, login Run entry and Start-menu shortcut were unchanged. Settings showed "Thalvi 0.1.4 is up to date. Updated to 0.1.4."
  - While a hold was down, a ready 0.1.5-dev.8 waited 75 s and installed about 12 s after the hold ended.
  - Switching back to Stable stayed on 0.1.5-dev.8 with the note above. Afterwards the released 0.1.2 and its config were put back.
- **Hyprland:**
  - Trial 0.1.3, paused, replaced its AppImage with 0.1.4 after 19 s and came back paused. The log shows one "Stopped." before each new process.
  - Settings showed "Updated to 0.1.4", and the login line still names the AppImage.
  - Switching to Development updated to 0.1.5-dev.8 in 11 s. Switching back to Stable left the file unchanged.
  - The metrics recorded check, download (about 9.9 s) and install.
  - With the version fix, trial 0.1.4 on Development updated to 0.1.5-dev.10 in 20 s. Settings showed "Updated to 0.1.5-dev.10", and the install metric recorded `0.1.5-dev.10`.
  - On that build, one app process ran. A hold dictation typed "Testing the overlay" into the target window, and the app-menu entry Thalvi wrote (`Exec="/home/rig/Apps/Thalvi.AppImage"`) opened Settings.

## Verification

- Gates on the integrated branch: `gates server` (with the spotter test models seeded; the first run timed out downloading them from modelscope.cn), `gates desktop-ui`, `gates release` and `cargo deny` pass. After the version fix, clippy is clean and `cargo test -p thalvi-app --lib` passes (156).

The worker removed each guard and confirmed a named test failed.
- Final check (verifier GPT-6.1 Terra). Every acceptance case passed through tests and probes, and a manual check during a download joined it. The plugin source showed signature and signed-version verification before install. `formal-capture-cancel` passes with the restart request modelled (22,275 states), with its negative controls and the real-code replay. `formal-config-save` passes (131 states per invariant) with no model change. Its minor finding is noted below.
- On Windows the update itself is verified, but the dictation clip's spoken ending wasn't heard ("No ending heard"), so a paste after an update is shown only on Hyprland.
- cargo-mutants (advisory): each survivor got a test or an exclusion with its reason. The new tests cover the channel names in metrics, a zero-length download, the marker's place beside the config, and a

## Problem

Writing used a fixed system prompt that told the model the user's speech is "never a request to you". That conflicted with explicit drafting requests: asking for an email sometimes produced only a cleaned-up sentence. Users could not adapt the instructions to their style or model without editing source and rebuilding.

## Change

- **Setting:** Settings → Speech → Writing has an editable multiline **Writing prompt**, with **Restore default prompt**. It is the system message of every writing call; the recognized words stay the user message, with no other context.
- **New default:** follows explicit requests for a kind of text (an email, a message), a tone or a wording, and answers in one paragraph without line breaks, because typed text refuses control characters and a line break would press Enter. It keeps every fact, name and number, adds no sentences, offers, promises or placeholders, and replies with the finished text only.
- **Storage:** `writing.prompt` is stored only when it differs from the default, so users who never edited it get later default improvements. A blank prompt is refused with "writing.prompt must not be blank. Restore the default to start over." The same check runs in Settings, on config load, and in the local agent surface (`settings get/check/set`), which shows the effective prompt and keeps the API key masked.
- **Docs:** a new DECISIONS bullet records the stored-override choice, and the README Writing section describes the prompt.

Saving never calls the model. Streaming, cancellation, the 15 s bound, clipboard recovery and paste without Enter are unchanged.

## Platforms

Hyprland (sandboxed nested rig, real Settings window and agent surface): implementer and an independent verifier, who also dictated through the real app into a local CPU model. GNOME and Windows: not used.

## Verification

- **Tests:** a fake-endpoint test observes the saved prompt as the system message and the words as the user message. Other tests cover blank refusal, normalizing the default away, legacy configs without the field, the agent surface with the key masked, and the UI's save, reopen, restore and validation. Each guard was removed in turn and its test failed.
- **Gates (implementer):** `cargo fmt`, `cargo lint`, `cargo test --workspace` (718 passed), `cargo docs` and the desktop UI gates pass. `cargo mutants --in-diff`: 8 mutants, 6 caught, 2 unviable, 0 survived. The server and desktop-ui gates are rerunning on this branch.
- **Rig, Settings:**
  - default shown with Restore disabled
  - edit, save, reopen and restart keep the prompt
  - Restore + Save removes `prompt` from `desktop.json`
  - the editor is readable in the dark looks after a CSS fix
- **Local CPU models** (qwen3 4B instruct, llama3.2 3B; two runs each, loopback only, no paid APIs):
  - The old wording invented commitments ("I will respond to your messages upon my return") and placeholders.
  - With the final default, "write this into an email: I have an appointment today and will not be in the office." gave a subject line and the same body, with nothing invented.
  - A short message and plain text kept their wording.
  - How closely a model follows the prompt is model-specific, and the README says so.
- **Independent verifier (GPT-6.1 Terra)**, real app in the rig with Qwen3 4B on CPU behind a request logger:
  - A custom "Reply in German." is sent as exactly the system message with the recognized words as the user message, and its German answer is typed without Enter.
  - Restore + Save removes `prompt` from the config, and the next request carries the default.
  - Saving makes no request.
  - A stopped model types nothing, puts the words on the clipboard and tells the user; the retry types.
  - A blank prompt is refused in Settings, `settings check`/`set` and on load.
  - `settings get` hides the key.
  - The editor is readable in holo and neon at both widths.
- **Bug found and fixed in this PR:** the first default asked for an email as a subject line, then the body. The model then answered with line breaks, which typed delivery refuses, so the email was never typed. The default now asks for one paragraph. After the fix, the email request was typed as one line in 3 of 3 real-app runs, and no reply contained a line break.
- **Model limit:** with the final default, Llama 3.2 3B (direct calls) answered the email request correctly once and in 2 of 3 runs asked for details already given or contradicted them. Small local models follow the prompt unevenly; Qwen3 4B followed it every time.
- **Not verified:** cancelling during a stream, the 15 s bound in the real app (both unchanged and covered by engine tests), and Windows.

Closes #288

## Problem

The runner's controls (cancel, pause, resume, Apply, update restart, quit) can arrive at any point of a capture. Until now each order that matters was a hand-written test, and `formal-capture-cancel` checks one capture with at most three controls. Nothing explored long random sequences across many captures, which is where stuck states and "it typed after I cancelled" bugs hide.

## Change

- **A test seam in the runner (`refactor`).** `Runner` and `Session` now build their engine through a crate-private `Rig`, and open the microphone through an `Input`. `DesktopRig` and `Microphone` are the real implementations, and their bodies moved over unchanged. `EngineLink::start` keeps its signature. Internally it is now a private `wire` (channels and hold input) plus a run of the runner, so a test can run the real runner on its own paused clock. No production caller changes.
- **One property (`runner/controls.rs`).**
  - It drives the real `Runner`, `Engine` and `EngineLink` with the existing fakes (`FakeRecognizer`, `FakeWake`, `FakeCuePlayer`, `FakeFrames`) and a recording `TestHost`, on a paused tokio clock with no wall-time sleeps.
  - It draws weighted sequences of up to 80 actions: wake, hold down/up, speech, silence, recognizer ready/answer/fail, Cancel, ToggleListening, SetListening, Apply (a retune, a rebuild, or a microphone switch), RestartIfIdle, device loss, and Quit (always last when drawn).
  - After every step it checks five invariants: never stuck, cancel and pause win, delivered once, errors are told, quit ends.
  - Each capture's identity comes from the fake recognizer's connection. After each step the harness waits for in-flight delivery and history writes, which run on a single blocking thread, so every seed replays identically.
- **The bug the property found (`fix`).** A wake, then an Apply that rebuilds the engine, then going quiet, could leave the status on **Starting** while the runner was idle. The old engine's follower can stop on its closed level watch before it publishes the final state, and the new follower waited for a change instead of publishing its initial state. The new follower now publishes its initial state at once. The regression case is `rebuilding_after_an_unready_capture_publishes_the_new_engines_resting_state`. It fails without the fix with `the replacement engine never published its initial Listening state`.
- **Docs.**
  - `DECISIONS.md`: the property-test entry now names the runner controls.
  - The `formal-capture-cancel` and `formal-hold-keys` source hashes are resynced. The mapped functions keep their meaning.

Decisions taken for the developer:
- The test gets its `EngineLink` from the private `wire`, then uses only its public methods. I'm counting that as the issue's "public `EngineLink` API".
- `Done` counts as a resting status for "never stuck", along with Paused, Listening, Keyboard and Failed. The issue's list left `Done` out.
- Apply draws only changes that need no network. `RemoveChat` is not drawn, because it reaches the per-user model store.

## Platforms

- **Windows 11, real session.** An independent verifier ran a debug build of `41eba7f`; the harness-only repair after it touches no production code. Six cases passed:
  1. Startup reaches Listening with the real microphone open.
  2. A WAV fed as input is recognized and pasted once.
  3. Cancel during Capturing and during the Pending countdown delivers nothing and settles to Listening.
  4. Pause closes the microphone and resume reopens it.
  5. Rebuilding settings changes (ending pause, cues), made while idle, after a hold released too soon, and after a delivered capture, settle to Listening in about 5 s. None stays on Starting.
  6. Quit exits in 197 ms.
- Not covered there: speech into a physical microphone, a physical hold-key press, and the tray's Quit click. The command-line equivalents were used instead.
- **Hyprland and GNOME:** not used. Linux CI only.

## Verification

**Each invariant fails when the behaviour it guards is broken.** Default seed `20261115`, temporary breaks in `runner.rs`, reverted after each run, on the final harness:

| Invariant | Break | Shrunk sequence | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Never stuck | a finished capture stays `Mode::Delivering` | `Apply(Wake), Apply(Cues), HoldDown, Answer(false), Wake, HoldUp(300)` | `never stuck: delivery or history did not finish` |
| 2 Cancel and pause win | `Control::Cancel` no longer ends the capture | `Wake, Cancel, Answer(false), Wake, Wake, Wake` | `cancel and pause win: capture0 reached the host` |
| 3 Delivered once | an accepted capture is delivered twice | `Apply(Wake), Apply(Cues), HoldDown, Answer(false), Wake, HoldUp(300)` | `delivered once: capture0 reached the host twice` |
| 4 Errors are told | `fail` clears the notice | `DeviceLost` | `errors are told: empty notice` |
| 5 Quit ends | Quit is ignored while idle | `Wake` | `quit ends: the runner exceeded QUIT_TIMEOUT` |

- Invariant 2 also caught both cancellation mutants on seeds 1–10 at 2,000 cases each, 10 of 10 for each mutant. One mutant ignores Cancel in the control drain; the other ignores Cancel while Capturing.
- With the correct code restored, every run passes.

**Runs:**
- **Default property:** 256 cases, about 9 s locally. `cargo test -p thalvi-app` runs 227 tests.
- **Exploratory run:** `PROPTEST_CASES=10000 PROPTEST_RNG_SEED=202611171725 cargo test -p thalvi-app --lib random_controls` on `9a0f69b`: **passed**, 10,000 cases in 436 s. An earlier version of the harness also passed 10,000 cases on seed `202611170525`.
- **Repair runs:** the repaired harness also passed 2,000 cases each on seeds 1, 2, 3 and `202611170525`.

**Review.** An independent review found that the first harness could charge a Cancel to the wrong capture, because it sampled the status while delivery ran on a blocking thread. candidates.body:
## Problem

On-device recognition only ran on the CPU. Nemotron Unified re-reads its last 6 s every 160 ms, so it keeps about 3 cores busy, and when another program loads the machine, words appear seconds late. A computer with a discrete GPU could run it much faster, but Thalvi never used the GPU. The user also couldn't see which hardware recognized their speech. #282 measured the options; this PR follows its recommendation.

## Change

On Linux, Nemotron Unified runs on a discrete GPU through ONNX Runtime's WebGPU backend. Everywhere else it runs on the CPU, and Settings says why.

**Choosing the device, at model load:**
- Dawn's adapter check (`wgpuInstanceRequestAdapter` and `wgpuAdapterGetInfo`) runs first. Only a discrete adapter counts: integrated GPUs and llvmpipe were slower than the CPU in #282.
- The session uses the WebGPU EP with `error_on_failure()`.
- A placement check reads ORT's own node assignment:
  - the encoder must have at least 98 % of its nodes on WebGPU;
  - no session may leave a compute op on the CPU.

**When the GPU isn't used:**
- Each fallback is one of six typed reasons, shown in Settings → Speech:
  - no usable GPU;
  - the GPU driver failed to start;
  - the model can't run fully on the GPU;
  - this model runs on the CPU;
  - GPU recognition isn't supported on Windows yet;
  - the GPU model isn't downloaded.
- Both speech metrics record the device and the reason. `desktop_speech_load` also records the placement counts.
- A model error during a capture drops the loaded model, so the next capture loads and picks a device again.

**Model files:**
- The GPU runs a new fp16 export from `export_unified_onnx.py --fp16`. It's reproducible byte for byte, and the tool versions are pinned. It's published as [`speech-models-v2`](https://github.com/NotPellew/Thalvi/releases/tag/speech-models-v2), 1.3 GB.
- The CPU keeps the int8 files from v1.
- A GPU machine that already has the int8 files starts on the CPU at once. Settings then offers the GPU download, and the next load uses the GPU.

**Packaging and scope:**
- `ort` features `webgpu`, `api-24` and `copy-dylibs` are on for Linux only.
- The AppImage ships `libwebgpu_dawn.so` (12.4 MB) and finds it through rpath.
- The DECISIONS.md static-binaries bullet is edited, and a WebGPU bullet is added.
- Nemotron Streaming and Parakeet stay on the CPU; #282 found them no faster on any GPU.
- Windows stays on the CPU (#317): its WebGPU build needs MSVC 14.50 or newer, and `windows-latest` has 14.44.
- The GPU session holds about 1.3 GB of VRAM while the model is loaded.

Closes #283
Refs #282, #281

## Platforms

**Hyprland:** the packaged AppImage from this branch, run in the verify-thalvi nested Hyprland on the developer's PC (RTX 5070 Ti, integrated Radeon, llvmpipe), with a synthetic voice on a private microphone. Cases:
- GPU files on disk;

## Problem

The conversation server sent every message and every piece of reply audio to the browser without a deadline, and those sends run inside the session's loop. When a browser stopped reading (a throttled background tab, a stalled network), a send blocked forever: the session never read the user's Stop, the reply could not be interrupted, and the session stayed open until the socket itself closed.

## Change

Every send to the browser now goes through one helper bounded by `BROWSER_SEND_WAIT` (2 s, the deadline the closing message already had). A send that times out or fails means the browser is gone: the session takes the same path as a disconnect (the reply is cut off, the conversation is saved and released), sends nothing more, and logs one `browser gone` warning with the reason. The send helpers now return `Result<(), BrowserGone>`, so a failed send can't be ignored silently. The session loop moved into `run_session`, which takes any sink and stream so a test can stall the browser side, and the conversation-takeover model's source map follows that move.

## Platforms

n/a (server only)

## Verification

- New test `a_browser_that_stops_receiving_ends_the_session_within_one_deadline` (paused clock, a sink that hangs and one that fails): fails on the unfixed code (`Elapsed`), passes now; the session ends at 2 s, the model stream is dropped, and no further send is attempted.
- Real server on the `verify-thalvi` fake endpoints, with a scripted client that stops reading mid-reply after audio frames start: on this branch the session ended 4.36 s after the reads stopped (deadline plus socket buffering), with one `browser gone … a send timed out` warning; the model stream was cancelled, and a fresh client reopened the conversation with the user turn and the partial reply saved. The same script against `development` (3d50a1c): no end in 35 s of no reads; the session only closed when the client closed its socket.
- Web client on fake endpoints: a typed conversation with spoken reply, Stop mid-reply, reload and reopen all behave as before.
- `formal-conversation-takeover`: passes (1,022,433 states, 371,796 distinct; one conversation, three connections, one turn each) after updating its source map; the model's `Close` already allowed this exit.
- `.github/scripts/gates server`: passes. Earlier runs failed only in `thalvi-desktop` spotter tests that timed out downloading their model from modelscope.cn into a fresh target dir; unrelated to this change, and green once the cache was warm.
- cargo-mutants on the diff: 26 caught, 2 timeouts (hangs, counted as caught), 2 missed: `BrowserGone`'s `Display` (log text only) and the existing `!state.reply_audio` guard, whose return type changed but whose behaviour is untouched and was already untested at session level.
- Not verified: a real browser tab being throttled; the stall was produced with a scripted client.

Closes #362

candidates.body:
## Problem

Thalvi typed dictation and writing key by key, so any line break would have pressed Enter. The text type refused every control character, and a multi-line writing reply failed with "The text contains control characters…". #307 worked around it by asking the model for one paragraph. Typing long text was also slow (about 140 ms for one sentence).

## Change

Delivery is a paste on Hyprland and Windows, for Paste, Write and Submit.

- `TypedText` becomes `PasteText`: it allows `\n` and `\t`, normalizes `\r\n` and lone `\r` to `\n`, and still refuses every other control character (C0, C1, ESC, DEL) where text enters.
- Hyprland: `deliver` copies with `wl-copy` first (the text is always left on the clipboard), refocuses and checks the bound window as before, then presses Ctrl+V, or Ctrl+Shift+V when the window class is in `TERMINAL_CLASSES` (kitty, foot, footclient, Alacritty, WezTerm, Ghostty, GNOME Console and Terminal, Konsole, Ptyxis, xterm). Submit adds the 250 ms pause and Return (`wtype -s 250 -k Return`).
- The paste keys are sent with `hyprctl dispatch sendshortcut`, not `wtype`. In the sandboxed Hyprland, GTK 3 (a hand-written TextView editor and the Settings webview) ignored `wtype -M ctrl -k v`: the key arrived with Control but hardware keycode 9 from wtype's own keymap, and no binding ran. `sendshortcut` uses the compositor's keymap and addresses the bound window. GTK 4, foot and kitty took both.
- `sendshortcut` is given the keycode of V (`code:N`), not the key name. Hyprland keeps the first keycode it finds for a name across layout changes (under dvorak, `v` and `x` kept their US keycodes and typed `k` and `q`, while names first used under dvorak were right) and fails a name with "key not found" while a virtual keyboard such as wtype's is the seat's keyboard. The keycode is read from the main keyboard's layout names in `hyprctl -j devices` with libxkbcommon (the `xkbcommon` crate, MIT, Linux only; libxkbcommon is already a GTK runtime dependency), in the first layout because `sendshortcut` sends the key with that layout's group even when another is active, and falls back to the key name when it cannot be read. When `input:kb_file` is set (`hyprctl -j getoption input:kb_file`), that file is compiled instead of the layout names, which do not describe it; an unreadable file or an unanswered option leaves the name `v` to Hyprland, whose worst result is a plain "key not found" notice with the text kept on the clipboard.
- Windows: copies with CRLF line breaks, keeps the process, integrity and front-window checks, then sends Ctrl+V (and Return) in one `SendInput` batch; after a partial batch it sends key-ups for every key it pressed and did not release. The Unicode key event path is deleted.
- GNOME stays clipboard only. The post-delivery copy in `delivery.rs` is gone because the host now leaves the text on the clipboard; `deliver` latency and outcome are still recorded.
- User-facing strings say pasted instead of typed, and when it is not known whether a paste happened they say so in plain words ("Thalvi may or may not have pasted the text. Check the window before trying again."). The writing `DEFAULT_PROMPT` now allows line breaks where the text needs them. README and DECISIONS are updated (new "Delivery is a paste", reworded "Check, then paste" and "Writing is one direct chat call").
- The formal-capture-cancel model's hashes and its replay expectation (`["deliver"]` instead of `["deliver", "copy"]`) are updated; admission through `Delivery::finish` is unchanged.

Based on #307; merge after it.

## Platforms

- Hyprland: used in the sandboxed nested Hyprland rig (`verify-thalvi/desktop.md`) with the debug build, a fake streaming writing endpoint, a synthetic voice into the private microphone, and foot, kitty, GNOME Text Editor (GTK 4) and a GTK 3 TextView window as targets. Not used in a real session.
- GNOME: not used; unchanged code path (clipboard only), covered by its existing unit tests.
- Windows: not used. The Windows code is covered by the fake-based unit tests and the `desktop-windows` CI job only (I could not cross-compile it here and the laptop was offline). Still to check by hand: Notepad, a browser text field and Windows Terminal (which may ask to confirm a multi-line paste). Windows has no pause before Enter, as before; whether a terminal agent needs one there is unverified.

## Verification

- `gates server` (fmt, clippy, workspace tests, docs, AppImage build) and `gates desktop-ui` pass.
- `cargo mutants --in-diff` (27.1.0, throwaway HOME, no desktop session): 14 mutants, 9 caught, 5 unviable, 0 missed. Windows files are excluded by `.cargo/mutants.toml`.
- formal-capture-cancel: `check.py` PASS (15,896 states), `--self-test` PASS, `repro.py` PASS.
- Rig, real app, one capture each, all `Delivered.`:
  - Writing a multi-line reply (with a tab) landed as separate lines in GTK 4, GTK 3 and foot (bytes recorded: lines as `\r`, tab kept), and in a kitty and a foot bash prompt it was pasted without executing (bracketed paste; marker files not created).
  - Single-line dictation landed in foot, GTK 3 and GTK 4.
  - Submit ("echo hello world, submit") pasted once and pressed Enter once after it (`Echo Hello World\r`).
  - A bound window closed before release: "The original window closed. Nothing was pasted. Captured text is on the clipboard."; the clipboard held the text, metrics recorded `deliver` as `nothing_typed`.
  - `deliver` took about 9 ms for a paste (one sentence or an email) and 266 to 276 ms for a submit (250 ms of it is the pause), against about 138 ms to type one sentence with the previous build.
  - 40 back-to-back `wl-copy` plus paste runs into foot pasted the right text every time, so the forking `wl-copy` is ready before the key.
- Layouts (rig, real app, `hyprctl keyword input:kb_layout/kb_variant`, `switchxkblayout`): F9-style hold dictation pasted correctly on us, de, back to us, us dvorak, back to us, `us(dvorak),de` with either layout ac

## Problem

`gates server` failed on changes that don't touch the desktop, because the spotter tests download their keyword-spotter models from modelscope.cn and those downloads time out. The models went into `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/tmp/models`, so every fresh target dir (every dev-job run) fetched them again. Each parallel test also started its own download of every file, about 28 connections at once from a cold start. On 2026-11-10, 5 of 6 gate runs on #342/#350 and 3 of 4 on #362 failed this way.

## Change

- The spotter test fixture keeps the models in a per-user cache that outlives target dirs: `~/.cache/thalvi/test-models`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\thalvi\test-models` on Windows. A machine downloads them once, and again only when a model changes.
- It is one shared fixture per test process, so tests running in parallel share a single fetch of each file.
- The app's real model folder is never touched.
- CI's model cache steps (`server`, `desktop-windows`, mutants) now cache that folder. There is one cache per OS, because the path differs.

## Platforms

n/a for the app: this changes test fixtures and CI only. The Linux fixture ran on the agent VM. The Windows cache path is exercised only by this PR's `desktop-windows` job.

## Verification

- Cold run on the agent VM, with an empty cache and the tests in parallel, through a proxy that logged every connection: all 11 spotter tests passed. Each of the 4 model files was fetched exactly once, as one request to `www.modelscope.cn` and its redirect to the CDN.
- With the cache filled and the network cut: all 11 passed, with no request made.
- With an empty cache and the network cut: the failure still names the file and the host.
- `.github/scripts/gates server`: UI build, fmt, lint, `cargo test --workspace` and docs passed. The AppImage step fails on this VM's missing `glib-sys` build libraries (an environment limit, unrelated).
- Not verified: two consecutive `gates server` dev-job runs with fresh target dirs on the developer machine, where the second should download nothing.

Closes #375

## Goal

Catch focus loss and stale status indicators on failing or slow async Settings actions deterministically in `npm run explore` before they reach `main`.

## In Short

`crates/thalvi-app/ui/src/fake.ts` gains deterministic URL-driven fault and delay modes (such as failing model downloads, failing saves, and slow in-flight downloads), and `crates/thalvi-app/ui/explore/settings.ts` runs regression and exploration traces against those modes under `focusNotDropped`, `progressEnds`, `refusalsSayWhy`, and a new in-flight status invariant.

```text
before: explore/settings.ts -> ?fake (happy-path downloads & saves only)
                            -> #594 (focus lost on failed download) & #593 (stale "Not downloaded") escape CI

after:  explore/settings.ts -> ?fake (happy path) + ?fake&fail=... + ?fake&slow=...
                            -> error & in-flight states checked for focus, status consistency, and error wording
```

## Problem & Current Context

- `explore/settings.ts` already asserts `focusNotDropped`, `progressEnds`, `refusalsSayWhy`, and `controlsHaveNames` in headless Chromium, and runs in both PR `desktop-ui` and Heavy `explore`.
- `fakeBackend` in `crates/thalvi-app/ui/src/fake.ts` currently returns happy-path results for downloads and most async commands, so error-handling and slow in-flight UI transitions are never exercised by `explore/settings.ts`.
- Open bugs #594 (keyboard focus lost after a failed wake-model download) and #593 (wake model row keeps saying "Not downloaded" with Download enabled while downloading) both break invariants the explorer is designed to enforce.

## Specification

1. **Deterministic fault/delay parameters in `crates/thalvi-app/ui/src/fake.ts`:**
   - Parse explicit query parameters in `fakeBackend(params)`:
     - `fail=<op[,op...]>`: deterministic failures for `wake-download`, `speech-download`, `save`, and `update-check` (returning realistic typed error strings, never uncaught exceptions).
     - `slow=<op[,op...]>`: deterministic delayed completion driven by the page clock (e.g. 2,000 ms under Playwright's fake clock, so `wait` steps observe the in-flight state cleanly without wall-clock sleeps).
   - Keep default `?fake` (without `fail`/`slow`) unchanged so existing regressions keep their exact behavior.
2. **Invariants & regressions in `crates/thalvi-app/ui/explore/settings.ts`:**
   - Add named regressions in `REGRESSIONS` covering:
     - Failed wake-model download (`fail=wake-download`) triggered via keyboard (`Tab`/`Return`): `focusNotDropped` holds (focus stays on a usable control, never `body`) and a visible error message is shown.
     - Slow in-flight wake-model download (`slow=wake-download`): while in flight, the row's status reflects downloading (never "Not downloaded") and the Download button is not re-triggerable; after the clock advances past completion, progress ends cleanly.
     - Failed settings save (`fail=save`): `focusNotDropped` and visible refusal wording hold.
   - Include at least one fault-injected exploration pass in `explore()` (using the same deterministic seed) so random interaction sequences also exercise error/in-flight paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fake.ts` supports deterministic `fail=` and `slow=` parameters covered by Vitest unit tests in `crates/thalvi-app/ui/src/settings.test.ts`.
- [ ] `npm run explore --prefix crates/thalvi-app/ui` runs the new fault/delay regressions and exploration pass and passes 3× in a row with no wall-clock sleeps.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (focus loss):** temporarily removing focus restoration on a failed wake-model download causes `npm run explore` to fail on `focusNotDropped`.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (stale status):** temporarily leaving the wake-model row at "Not downloaded" during an in-flight download causes `npm run explore` to fail on the in-flight status check.
- [ ] `.github/scripts/gates desktop-ui` passes.

## Sub-issues / Related

- Depends on #593 and #594 (both live bugs on `main` must be fixed before the new regression assertions can pass).

## Goal

Measure the post-#416 CI/CD critical path and parallelize Windows packaging only if it saves at least two minutes of median wall time while adding no more than one Windows runner-minute per run.

## In Short

The fast PR tier and heavy `main` tier already exist. The remaining observed critical path is the serial Windows format/lint/test/package job followed by installed-app smoke. This issue first establishes a representative baseline, then tries one bounded change: package the NSIS installer in parallel with the Windows checks while keeping smoke afterward.

If comparable runs do not meet the agreed two-minute/one-runner-minute rule, the result is a documented no-go and the serial workflow stays unchanged.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Measure comparable PR and heavy runs] --> B{Median saves at least 2 min and adds at most 1 Windows runner-minute?}
  B -->|No| C[Record no-go; keep serial CI]
  B -->|Yes, projected| D[Run Windows checks and packaging in parallel]
  D --> E[Installed-app smoke after both succeed]
  E --> F[Compare real before/after runs against the same rule]
```

## Problem & Current Context

#416 already made PR steps change-aware and moved diff-scoped mutation testing to the heavy tier. #421 addressed avoidable local work. The original pre-split description is no longer the baseline.

Two recent samples identify, but do not prove, the current opportunity:

- [Heavy run 43415492925](https://github.com/NotPellew/Thalvi/actions/runs/43415492925) on 55cca7ec: Windows CI ran about 7m26s, smoke another 34s, and the slowest mutant shard finished before Windows. Creation-to-start waiting is separate from execution.
- [PR run 43413421684](https://github.com/NotPellew/Thalvi/actions/runs/43413421684): Windows CI ran about 6m56s and smoke another 37s.

`.github/scripts/gates` currently serializes Windows checks and NSIS packaging. `desktop-windows-smoke` depends on that job's installer. Release packages embed their selected version and have separate signing, approval, and heavy-run safeguards; ordinary CI artifacts cannot be substituted for them.

## Specification / Architectural Contract

### Baseline and go rule

- Sample recent comparable desktop-affecting PRs and full heavy runs, targeting at least five of each where available. Record run links, queue time, job durations, cache conditions, package/smoke time, failures/retries, and summed runner minutes. State small or missing samples explicitly.
- Separate queueing and release approval from execution. Do not claim savings from cancelled, incomplete, or reduced-coverage runs.
- Project the change's median wall-time benefit and extra Windows runner cost from the baseline. Proceed only when the projection supports at least **2 minutes saved** and at most **1 additional Windows runner-minute per run**.

### Bounded implementation if the rule is met

- Split only Windows CI packaging from the Windows format/lint/test path so they can run concurrently. Keep every existing command and the same pinned toolchains; `.github/scripts/gates` remains the single source of those commands.
- Preserve the required `desktop-windows` and `desktop-windows-smoke` contexts. Smoke runs only after checks and packaging both succeed, installs the NSIS artifact from the tested commit, and opens Settings.
- Packaging failure, cancellation, or a missing installer must make the appropriate required status fail, never become a skipped green or a hanging check.
- Affected-path PR behavior, always-on checks, heavy full coverage, mutation feedback, cache rules, and `verified` advancement remain intact.
- Leave release versioning, artifact signing, publication approval, and release gating unchanged. Do not publish solely for a benchmark.
- If the real before/after runs miss the go rule, revert to the serial orchestration and record the no-go rather than keeping a costly change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A linked baseline reports representative run links, sample sizes, queue versus execution, cache conditions, critical path, and runner minutes, plus the projection used for the go/no-go decision.
- [ ] If implemented, comparable before/after Actions runs show at least 2 minutes lower median wall time and at most 1 added Windows runner-minute per run; variability is reported. Otherwise the issue records why no orchestration change landed.
- [ ] Live test PRs for an app change and a `Cargo.lock` change run every affected Linux/Windows gate, produce an installer from the tested commit, and pass installed-app smoke. An unaffected change and the existing change-detector fallback still behave safely.
- [ ] Controlled Actions runs force Windows test, packaging, missing-artifact, and smoke failures separately. Each blocks the appropriate required status; cancellation cannot falsely pass or leave a required check pending.
- [ ] A full heavy run preserves mutation feedback and advances `verified` only after every required component succeeds.
- [ ] Release safeguards and package paths are inspected and applicable non-publishing checks pass; no release is published for measurement.
- [ ] No required test, lint/type/format/docs check, dependency or secret scan, Linux/Windows package, Windows smoke, or mutation feedback is removed.

## Sub-issues / Related

- #406/#416 established the fast/heavy CI tiers.
- #404 owns local staging; #421 owns the completed local heavy-run reductions.
- #422 owns the docs-only PR selection fix independently.
- #382 owns spotter model-cache reuse independently.
- #352 owns Windows Authenticode signing separately.

candidates.body:
## Goal

Prevent PRs from silently weakening existing tests or running against outdated CI rules from an old `main` branch point.

## In Short

Port two lightweight PR checks from Vardli into Thalvi's `.github/workflows/commits.yml` and `.github/scripts/`:
1. **`tests-explained` (`changed-tests`):** fails a PR if it edits or deletes an existing test function (Rust `#[test]` / TypeScript `test(`/`it(` / Python `def test_`) without naming each changed test and why it changed under a `Changed tests` section in the PR description.
2. **`ci-current`:** fails a PR if `main` changed CI, lint, or formal-check files since the PR branched off `main`, forcing a merge/rebase onto current `main` before merging.

```text
PR opened/updated
  ├── tests-explained: edited/deleted existing test? -> must be listed with reason under "Changed tests"
  └── ci-current:      main touched .github/, Cargo.toml, clippy.toml, deny.toml, formal-*/ since fork point? -> must merge main
```

## Problem & Current Context

- Thalvi's `.github/workflows/commits.yml` currently checks only `semantic-title` and `commit-messages`.
- Nothing in CI flags a PR that edits or deletes an existing test assertion to make a gate pass, and nothing forces a long-lived PR branch to pick up newly merged CI or lint checks from `main` before merging.
- Vardli already enforces both via `scripts/changed-tests` (`tests-explained` in `commits.yml`) and `scripts/ci-current` (in `gates-always.yml`).

## Specification

1. **`tests-explained` (`.github/scripts/changed-tests` + `commits.yml` job):**
   - Inspect `BASE_SHA..HEAD_SHA` for edits to or removals of existing tests in Rust (`crates/**/*.rs`), TypeScript (`crates/thalvi-app/ui/**/*.test.ts`, `explore/settings.ts` `REGRESSIONS`), and Python (`speech/**/*.py`). Adding brand-new tests requires no entry.
   - When any existing test is modified or deleted, require the PR body to contain a `Changed tests` heading naming each changed test with a non-empty reason; otherwise exit non-zero listing the unexplained tests.
   - Update `.github/pull_request_template.md` with a brief optional `## Changed tests` hint if not already present.
2. **`ci-current` (`.github/scripts/ci-current` + `commits.yml` job):**
   - Fetch `origin main` (no tags) and compare `git merge-base FETCH_HEAD "$HEAD_SHA"` against `FETCH_HEAD` for: `.github`, `.cargo`, `.githooks`, `Cargo.toml`, `clippy.toml`, `deny.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.agents/skills/formal-*/`.
   - Exit non-zero listing the changed CI/gate files on `main` when non-empty.
3. **Unit tests & gates:**
   - Add unit tests for both scripts (covering added vs modified vs deleted tests, explained vs unexplained PR bodies, stale vs up-to-date fork points) and run them in `.github/scripts/gates issue-sync` (or `release`/a scripts gate) and `shellcheck` if shell scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests for `.github/scripts/changed-tests` and `.github/scripts/ci-current` pass locally and in CI.
- [ ] `tests-explained` and `ci-current` jobs run on `pull_request` (`opened`, `edited`, `synchronize`, `reopened`) in `.github/workflows/commits.yml`.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (`tests-explained`):** in a test fixture, modifying an existing Rust or Vitest test with an empty PR body fails with the test name; adding it under `Changed tests` with a reason passes; adding a brand-new test passes with no `Changed tests` section.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (`ci-current`):** in a temp git repo, committing a change to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on `main` after a branch forks fails `ci-current`; merging `main` into the branch makes it pass.
- [ ] `.github/scripts/gates` passes.

## Sub-issues / Related

- Related: #513 (CODEOWNERS on CI and formal checks).

https://github.com/NotPellew/Thalvi/actions/runs/45588704722 failed on `main` at ce44756282b71d0866c1be937d6368a184f97775 (first report). Later failures are in the comments below.

## Goal

Heavy's `mutants` jobs pass on `main` again, by testing the behavior the surviving mutant shows is untested.

## In Short

One mutant survives on `main` (heavy runs 45891088955 and 45900430252, shard 0): in `Publisher::mutate` (`crates/thalvi-app/src/runner.rs:495`), `*current != state.view.rebuilding` replaced with `==` passes every test. So no test checks that the "rebuilding" watch notifies subscribers when the value changes and stays quiet when it does not. Those notifications drive the Settings "rebuilding" event (`crates/thalvi-app/src/app.rs:1114`). The fix adds that check to the existing test.

```text
mutant: changed = *current == state.view.rebuilding
today:  a_queued_rebuild_is_published_while_the_capture_keeps_its_status → passes (mutant survives)
after:  the same test asserts a notification on false→true and true→false, none for an unchanged value → fails on the mutant

candidates.body:
## Problem

Thalvi already has a shared Clippy gate, behavioral tests, formal checks, cargo-deny and diff-scoped mutation testing. The missing pieces are targeted enforcement of production panic/todo and redundant clones, repeatable property-test inputs, and a documented unused-dependency audit. Enabling every nursery lint instead would introduce substantial style noise.

## Desired outcome

### Goal

Tighten the existing verification workflow while keeping it small, reproducible and consistent between local work and CI.

### In Short

Developers keep using the existing gates. Production unwrap/expect/panic/todo and unnecessary clones fail lint; intentional test operations retain narrow, reasoned exceptions. Property tests default to repeatable cases, with explicit seed overrides for exploration. An advisory dependency command identifies unused direct dependencies.

```text
cargo lint        -> enforced, targeted Rust checks
cargo test        -> 256 property cases, fixed ChaCha seed by default
cargo deps-audit  -> advisory cargo-machete report
existing gates    -> shared local/CI verification
```

### Specification

- Deny unwrap_used, expect_used, panic and todo; add redundant_clone to the warnings-as-errors gate. Retain test exemptions and narrowly justified expectations, without allow shims.
- Keep existing numeric checks and unsafe deny with documented native FFI exceptions. Do not add blanket indexing bans, all nursery lints, or lower hard complexity caps.
- Default proptest to 256 ChaCha cases with seed 20261115; permit recorded seed overrides for exploratory runs and preserve minimized regressions.
- Add advisory cargo deps-audit using cargo-machete 0.9.2; retain cargo-deny and the existing mutation/formal workflows.
- Resolve observed redundant clones and the unused desktop tracing-subscriber dependency without weakening tests. Refresh the config-save source hash for test-only edits and rerun its check/self-test.
- Document prerequisites and exception policy in AGENTS.md and reconcile the unsafe boundary in DECISIONS.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] cargo lint passes for the workspace with the frontend prerequisite built; intentional test clone/panic behavior remains tested.
- [ ] cargo deps-audit reports no unused dependencies; cargo-deny advisories, licences and sources pass.
- [ ] The existing Linux component gates pass, including AppImage packaging, web, desktop UI, speech, issue-sync, release and formal hashes.
- [ ] Config-save bounded verification passes, and its self-test detects every mutation.
- [ ] Full Rust tests pass with the configured property-test defaults; ignored/device-dependent cases are reported separately.
- [ ] Gitleaks passes for history and the changes.
- [ ] The PR Windows CI gate passes on the same head; Linux checks are not reported as Windows or native desktop qualification.

## Context and related issues

Agreed through a repository-specific audit and design discussion. This is one verification-policy improvement, not a new harness framework. Implementation is already prepared; the companion PR will close this issue. Existing Linux verification passed on the exact prepared tree; Windows remains for PR CI. No external models, recordings or paid endpoints are required for the local checks.

## Goal

Make it impossible by construction—and formally checked in `formal-capture-cancel`—for a post-confirmation recognizer merge to overwrite or bypass cleanup on text the user already confirmed for Submit delivery.

## In Short

Once the user confirms a Submit capture, the confirmed (and cleaned, when dictation cleanup is on) text becomes an immutable typed value (`ConfirmedDelivery`) that extra-recognizer merge or re-transcription cannot overwrite, and `formal-capture-cancel` gains an invariant asserting that a confirmed Submit delivers the exact cleaned text shown at confirmation.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Raw[Live + extra recognizers] --> Clean[Cleanup pass when enabled]
    Clean --> Confirm[User confirms Submit]
    Confirm --> Lock[ConfirmedDelivery immutable text]
    Late[Late merge / re-transcribe] -. blocked by type & invariant .-> Lock
    Lock --> Deliver[Delivery pastes exact confirmed text]
```

## Problem & Current Context

- Open bug #537 (*paste cleaned text when extra recognizers merge after you confirm*) showed that with Clean up dictation enabled and extra recognizers active, a merge running after confirmation could replace the confirmed, cleaned text with uncleaned merged text.
- Upcoming features #586 (*re-transcribe finished capture and replace live text*) and #589 (*extra recognizers without chat-model merge*) add more post-capture text replacement paths in `crates/thalvi-desktop/src/engine.rs` (`conclude`, `merge`, `clean`, `prepare_submit`) and `delivery.rs`.
- `formal-capture-cancel` currently proves that cancellation blocks delivery (`NoDeliveryAfterStop`, `ExtrasNeverLeftOpen`, `ReleasedWhenCancelled`, `LateOnlyAfterMerge`, `AcceptedOnlyAfterLoad`), but has no invariant over *which* text (confirmed/cleaned vs late-merged) reaches delivery.

## Specification

1. **Type-level guard in `crates/thalvi-desktop/src/engine.rs` & `delivery.rs`:**
   - Introduce a narrow, unforgeable type (e.g. `ConfirmedDelivery` / sealed newtype constructed only at the confirmation boundary after any required cleanup/merge) carrying the final Submit text.
   - Ensure late extra-recognizer merges or re-transcription results cannot mutate or replace a `ConfirmedDelivery` once confirmation has occurred (any merge/cleanup that applies to Submit must finish before constructing `ConfirmedDelivery`, or late merges are discarded/ignored after confirmation).
2. **Formal invariant in `.agents/skills/formal-capture-cancel/`:**
   - Extend `CaptureCancel.tla` (from the real code after #537 lands) to track whether a Submit was confirmed with cleaned text and whether a merge/replacement ran before vs after confirmation.
   - Add an invariant (e.g. `ConfirmedTextDeliveredUnchanged`) asserting that every delivered Submit delivers the exact text confirmed (cleaned when cleanup is enabled), never overwritten by a post-confirmation merge.
   - Add a negative-control mutation in `.agents/skills/formal-capture-cancel/scripts/check.py` (`--self-test`) that reintroduces post-confirmation overwrite and must violate `ConfirmedTextDeliveredUnchanged`.
   - Update `source.json`, `view.py`, `chart.mmd`, and `SKILL.md` (`Property`, `Covers`, `Run`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A confirmed Submit passes through a dedicated immutable type (`ConfirmedDelivery` or equivalent) constructed only once final pre-confirmation merge/cleanup is settled; no post-confirmation code path can substitute its text.
- [ ] Unit/integration tests in `crates/thalvi-desktop` prove that a late extra-recognizer merge arriving after confirmation cannot overwrite the confirmed cleaned text.
- [ ] `.agents/skills/formal-capture-cancel/scripts/check.py` and `--self-test` pass, with the new invariant (`ConfirmedTextDeliveredUnchanged`) passing on the faithful model and failing on its negative-control mutation.
- [ ] `.agents/skills/formal-capture-cancel/scripts/check.py chart` succeeds and `chart.mmd` is updated.
- [ ] `.github/scripts/gates server` and `.github/scripts/gates formal` pass.

## Sub-issues / Related

- Depends on #537 (fixes the live post-confirmation merge bug first).
- Related: #586 (re-transcribe finished capture), #589 (extra recognizers without chat-model merge).

candidates.body:
## Goal

Prevent agents or PRs from quietly silencing Rust clippy lints with new `#[allow(...)]` or `#[expect(...)]` attributes by enforcing a ratcheting budget in CI.

## In Short

Thalvi already denies `allow_attributes_without_reason` and ratchets OS `cfg` uses via `.github/scripts/rust-layout.allow`, but `allow_attributes` is only `warn` and `#[expect(...)]` counts are untracked (`crates/` currently has 0 `#[allow(...)]` and 132 `#[expect(...)]` sites).

After this change:
- `Cargo.toml` sets `allow_attributes = "deny"` under `[workspace.lints.clippy]`.
- A new `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions` check (ported from Vardli's `scripts/lint-exceptions`) counts every `#[expect]` / `#![expect]` in `crates/` (including inside `cfg_attr` and `r#expect`, ignoring comments/strings) against `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions.toml`.
- Going over a lint's budget fails CI and lists every `file:line`; going under fails until the budget is lowered, so exceptions only ever decrease unless explicitly raised in review.

```text
before: new #[expect(clippy::...)] in crates/ -> passes CI silently
after:  new #[expect(clippy::...)] in crates/ -> lint-exceptions gate fails until fixed or budget raised in .github/scripts/lint-exceptions.toml
```

## Problem & Current Context

- `Cargo.toml:19` sets `allow_attributes = "warn"` (and `crates/` already has 0 `#[allow(...)]` attributes on `main`).
- `crates/` currently has 132 `#[expect(...)]` attributes with no upper-bound check; agents can add new `#[expect(..., reason = "...")]` attributes to silence clippy warnings instead of fixing the underlying issue.
- Vardli already solves this cleanly with `scripts/lint-exceptions` + `ci/lint-exceptions.toml` + unit tests (`scripts/tests/test_lint_exceptions.py`).

## Specification

1. **Workspace lint:** Change `allow_attributes = "warn"` to `allow_attributes = "deny"` in `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.clippy]`).
2. **Exception budget checker:**
   - Add `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions` (Python 3 stdlib, lexer-aware so comments/string literals don't match, handles `#[expect(...)]`, `#![expect(...)]`, nested `cfg_attr`, raw `r#expect`/`r#cfg_attr`, and multi-lint attributes).
   - Add `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions.toml` initialized to the exact current counts on `main` (unlisted lints have budget 0).
   - Fail when any lint exceeds its budget (listing every `path:line`) OR falls below its budget (prompting to lower the budget in `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions.toml`).
3. **Tests & CI wiring:**
   - Add unit tests for `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions` (covering over-budget, under-budget, comments/strings ignored, `cfg_attr`, multi-lint attributes, malformed TOML).
   - Run `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions` and its unit tests in `.github/scripts/gates server` (and include it in `ci.yml` / `AGENTS.md` if applicable).
   - Ensure `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions.toml` falls under `/.github/` so #513's `CODEOWNERS` covers budget increases automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Cargo.toml` sets `allow_attributes = "deny"` and `cargo lint` passes on `main`.
- [ ] `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions` passes on `main` with `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions.toml` matching exact current counts (0 unlisted lints).
- [ ] Unit tests for `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions` pass and run in `.github/scripts/gates`.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (over budget):** adding one `#[expect(clippy::redundant_clone, reason = "test")]` in `crates/` makes `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions` exit non-zero and print its `file:line`.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (under budget):** raising any budget by 1 in `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions.toml` makes `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions` exit non-zero and instruct lowering it.
- [ ] `.github/scripts/gates server` passes.

## Sub-issues / Related

- Related: #513 (`/.github/` CODEOWNERS will automatically gate budget increases in `.github/scripts/lint-exceptions.toml`).
- Related: #508 (indexing lint rule).

## Goal

Catch narrow-width Settings layout regressions (overflow, clipping, and sibling overlap) deterministically in PR CI before they reach `main`.

## In Short

`gate_desktop_ui` in `.github/scripts/gates` gains a deterministic Chromium layout sweep across every Settings page—and each open add/edit form—at four window sizes: `400×680`, `640×850`, `780×680`, and `1280×900`. Every checked control must be visible, unoccluded, wholly inside the viewport (after vertical scroll only), and non-overlapping with every other non-nested control.

```text
before: gate_desktop_ui -> vitest + explore (1000x760 only, no box checks)
                           -> #592 (400x680 overflow) & #583 (640px overlap) ship to main

after:  gate_desktop_ui -> vitest + explore + Settings layout sweep (400x680, 640x850, 780x680, 1280x900)
                           -> overflow or sibling overlap fails PR CI at once
```

## Problem & Current Context

- `crates/thalvi-app/ui/explore/settings.ts` creates its Playwright context at a single wide viewport (`1000×760`) and checks focus, progress, refusals, and accessible names, never bounding-box containment or overlap.
- `.agents/skills/verify-thalvi/scripts/settings-boxes` already runs bounding-box containment, unoccluded, and pairwise non-overlap checks in headless Chromium against `settings.html?fake&at=0`, but `gate_desktop_ui` never invokes it.
- Two narrow-width regressions landed on `main` while `desktop-ui` passed: #592 (Recognition page Live recognizer drop-down overflows at `400×680`) and #583 (server add/edit form fields overlap the next label at `640×850`).

## Specification

1. **Checked surfaces:** Every Settings page reachable from `nav[aria-label="Settings pages"]`, plus the interactive forms that expand layout height/width:
   - Recognition: add/edit forms for streaming servers, after-you-stop servers, and extra-only servers, plus the on-device speech model editor;
   - Listening, Chat model (including Details expanded), Commands, History & recordings, and App.
2. **Checked viewports:** `400×680`, `640×850`, `780×680`, and `1280×900`.
3. **Geometry invariants per viewport** (matching `.agents/skills/verify-thalvi/scripts/settings-boxes`):
   - Scroll each visible control/label vertically into view only (reset any horizontal `scrollLeft` to `0` before measuring).
   - Every visible control and its label must have non-zero size, lie wholly within `[0, width] × [0, height]` (0.5 px tolerance), and be unoccluded at its centre.
   - No two non-nested visible controls/labels may overlap (0.5 px tolerance).
   - No horizontal overflow on the document or main scroll container (`scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 1`).
4. **Wiring:**
   - Expose the sweep as an npm script in `crates/thalvi-app/ui/package.json` (e.g. `npm run layout`) and call it from `gate_desktop_ui` in `.github/scripts/gates` after Chromium is installed.
   - Keep `.agents/skills/verify-thalvi/scripts/settings-boxes` working or have it share the same geometry helper so manual verification and CI cannot drift.
   - Print the failing viewport, page/form state, control label, and box coordinates on failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npm run layout --prefix crates/thalvi-app/ui` and `.github/scripts/gates desktop-ui` run the sweep across all Settings pages and open server/model forms at `400×680`, `640×850`, `780×680`, and `1280×900`, and exit 0 on the fixed tree.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (containment):** temporarily forcing a control wider than `400 px` on the Recognition page makes the sweep exit non-zero, naming the viewport (`400×680`), page, and overflowing control.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (overlap):** temporarily giving a server form field negative bottom margin so it overlaps the next label makes the sweep exit non-zero at `640×850`, naming both overlapping elements.
- [ ] Runs deterministically 3× in a row with no fixed sleeps and adds under 30 seconds to `desktop-ui`.

## Sub-issues / Related

- Depends on #583 and #592 (both live layout bugs on `main` must be fixed before this gate can go green).
- Related: `.agents/skills/verify-thalvi/scripts/settings-boxes`.

## Goal

Ensure Thalvi's CI actually executes its formal checks, verifies git provenance of `source.json`, runs negative controls (`--self-test`), and catches stale TLA+ statecharts instead of only comparing local file hashes.

## In Short

Today `.github/scripts/gates formal` only runs `formal-source-hashes.py`, which checks local SHA-256 hashes against `source.json`. It never checks whether `sync_commit` is an ancestor of `HEAD` holding those exact blobs, never runs TLC (`formal-capture-cancel`, `formal-config-save`) or the exhaustive Rust harness (`formal-hold-keys`), never runs `--self-test`, and never checks `chart.mmd` freshness.

After this change:
1. `formal-source-hashes.py` also verifies git provenance for every `formal-*/source.json` (resolving `sync_commit`, checking `merge-base --is-ancestor`, and checking each listed path's blob at `sync_commit` matches the recorded SHA-256—matching Vardli's provenance check).
2. PR CI runs each formal skill's `check.py` + `--self-test` + `chart` freshness check whenever the PR diff touches that skill's `Covers:` paths (or `.agents/skills/formal-*/`).
3. Heavy (`heavy.yml`) runs all three formal skills (`check.py`, `--self-test`, and `chart` freshness) unconditionally on `main`, nightly, and `workflow_dispatch`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    PR[PR diff] --> H[formal-source-hashes.py: file SHA-256 + git sync_commit provenance]
    PR --> C{Touches Covers: or formal-*/?}
    C -- no --> P[fast pass]
    C -- yes --> R[Run matching check.py + --self-test + chart diff]
    Heavy[Heavy on main/nightly] --> All[Run all 3 formal skills + --self-test + chart diff]
```

## Problem & Current Context

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`formal` job) calls `.github/scripts/gates formal`, which only executes `python3 .github/scripts/formal-source-hashes.py`.
- `formal-source-hashes.py` checks `root / relative` SHA-256 against `source.json`, but ignores `sync_commit` entirely—a bogus or non-ancestor `sync_commit` passes silently.
- Because CI never runs `check.py`, `--self-test`, or `check.py chart`, a PR can introduce a broken `.tla` invariant, a stale negative control, a broken `harness.rs`, or a stale `chart.mmd` and pass the `formal` gate.
- All three formal checks are already self-contained and fast warm: `formal-config-save` (~2.5 s), `formal-capture-cancel` (seconds), and `formal-hold-keys` (<1 min with warm Cargo cache).

## Specification

1. **Git provenance in `.github/scripts/formal-source-hashes.py`:**
   - Reject missing, malformed, all-zero, or non-commit `sync_commit` values.
   - Require `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sync_commit> HEAD` (workflow checkout for `formal` uses `fetch-depth: 0`; never fetch inside the script).
   - For every file in `source.json["files"]`, verify the blob at `<sync_commit>:<path>` has the exact recorded SHA-256, in addition to the working-tree check.
   - Clear git redirect env vars (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`) before invoking `git`.
   - Add unit tests for provenance failures (bogus commit, non-ancestor commit, mismatched blob at `sync_commit`, missing file) run by `.github/scripts/gates formal`.
2. **Run formal checks in `.github/scripts/gates` and CI:**
   - Cache `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/thalvi-formal` in `ci.yml` (keyed by TLC/JRE pin hashes in `formal-*/scripts/check.py`) so `tla2tools.jar` and Temurin JRE are not re-downloaded every run.
   - On `pull_request`, run `check.py` and `check.py --self-test` for every formal skill whose `Covers:` globs (or `.agents/skills/formal-<name>/`) match the PR diff; for `formal-hold-keys`, reuse the Linux Rust toolchain/cache (or run in a dedicated job with `rust-cache` + Linux deps).
   - On `workflow_call` (called by `heavy.yml` with `scope: all`), run all three formal skills unconditionally.
3. **Chart freshness:**
   - For each TLA+ formal skill (`formal-capture-cancel`, `formal-config-save`) that runs, run `check.py chart` into a temp path (or compare generated `chart.mmd` against the committed `chart.mmd`) and fail if `chart.mmd` differs.
   - Also run `python3 .agents/skills/formal-hold-keys/scripts/test_check.py` whenever `formal-hold-keys` runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `formal-source-hashes.py` unit tests cover valid provenance, non-ancestor `sync_commit`, blob-hash mismatch at `sync_commit`, and working-tree drift, and pass in `.github/scripts/gates formal`.
- [ ] A PR touching a covered file for `formal-config-save`, `formal-capture-cancel`, or `formal-hold-keys` executes that skill's `check.py`, `--self-test`, and (for TLA+) `chart.mmd` freshness check in CI.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (broken model):** temporarily breaking an invariant or negative control in a scratch branch/test causes the CI formal gate to exit non-zero.
- [ ] **Mutation proof (stale chart):** temporarily editing a line in `formal-config-save/chart.mmd` causes the chart freshness check to fail.
- [ ] A PR touching no covered formal paths still runs `formal-source-hashes.py` (with provenance) in under 30 seconds without invoking TLC or Cargo.
- [ ] Heavy (`heavy.yml`) runs all three formal skills unconditionally when `scope == all`.

## Sub-issues / Related

- Related: #513 (CODEOWNERS on CI and formal checks).
